news.title: Meta's Muse now calls businesses for you
news.description: Meta's AI agent Muse can now call businesses on behalf of paying US subscribers. The agent already has over 10 million users. Google Gemini, Instinct, and xAI's Grok Bot offer the same feature. Many businesses hang up as soon as they detect an AI on the line.

news.title: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative
news.description: US public-sector unions are increasingly pushing through protections against AI surveillance and automated firings. In Oakland, a strike vote forced retraining programs instead of layoffs, and a transport union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. California banned so-called bossware.

news.title: Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's
news.description: Jensen Huang likely left Nvidia more because of risky business practices than anything else, a Wall Street Journal report suggests. The company offered cloud providers billions in financial guarantees for chip purchases. Interim CEO and then-CFO Colette Kress tried to contain the risk, and Huang reportedly didn't like that.

news.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: The unfolding Huang
news.description: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. The 63-year-old admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond his personal life. U.S. officials believe one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information to Beijing.

news.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
news.description: LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG. That's more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago. LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole
news.description: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang steps down as CEO. Huang's departure leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions. Nvidia has been a prolific investor in startups and participated in 105 rounds this year alone. Huang’s departure could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. Some investors hope that large cloud companies and other chipmakers will step in to fill some of the void.

news.title: OpenAI enters the cybersecurity market with two Daybreak
news.description: Daybreak Red Team uses AI agents to automatically probe web applications for vulnerabilities. The tool also verifies reported security flaws from bug bounty programs and tests patches. The second product, Daybreak Defense Factory, automates the defensive side. Both products run on OpenAI's latest cyber model, GPT-6 Cyber, which runs on the GPT Cyber.

news.title: Anthropic's IPO is six times oversubscribed
news.description: Anthropic is on track for the largest IPO ever, with orders exceeding available shares by a factor of six. The developer and its co-founders aim to raise $64.4 billion through the public offering and $26 billion via a private placement. The target valuation sits at roughly $1.4 trillion, with existing investors getting priority in share allocation. The company's annualized revenue climbed to $81 billion by late October, up from $71 billion in September.

news.title: Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell
news.description: Former OpenAI researcher Will DePue says he has produced the first technical evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group are using Nvidia's latest Blackwell GPUs despite US export controls. His forensic method reads characteristic chip signatures directly from published model weights. He estimates the hardware behind the five training runs.

news.title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into
news.description: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugin connects the AI directly to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, and Infor. Its 17 specialized skills let the AI draft quotes, compare suppliers, and place backup orders when deliveries are delayed. The plugin doesn't control physical machines yet, but Anthropic is separately developing the.

news.title: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors
news.description: Banks reject buy orders from mainland China and Hong Kong, citing U.S. export control rules known as ITAR. Similar restrictions applied during SpaceX's IPO, and Anthropic's products aren't available in either region anyway.

news.title: OpenAI rebuilt AI shopping from scratch with ChatGPT
news.description: Users register a card once and confirm each purchase through Face ID or fingerprint. Actual card details stay hidden behind payment tokens. Rivals Anthropic, Meta, and xAI already have their agents making purchases.

news.title: Knowledge Transfer for Conditional Flow Matching: Frozen Estimation
news.description: Conditional generative modeling with limited target data can benefit from representations learned in a related source population. We develop a transfer learning framework for conditional flow matching that accommodates distinct source and target response distributions and dimensions. We establish bounds on conditional squared Wasserstein risk that account for source estimation, target fitting, representation mismatch, and numerical integration. We also develop independent validation procedure for selecting among fitted conditional generators.

news.title: SkinAdvisor: An AI-Driven Decision Framework for Skin Production
news.description: SkinAdvisor, an AI-driven decision framework for skin production planning, powered by SkinCast, a deployed multi-modal Transformer forecasting 180-day per-day sales trajectories for unreleased skins. SkinCast couples four encoders: a pretrained Informer for player-preference time series, a. pretrained Player-Hero-Skin graph embedder for relational priors, and two lightweight Transformers for skin attributes and release context, fused through a shared backbone with a local-plus-global day-x positional encoding.

news.title: EASTAR: Event-Anchored Semantic Semantic and Task-Adapt
news.description: Urban region representation learning supports a wide range of urban analytics tasks by encoding regional functions and interactions. EASTAR treats offline activity events as sparse semantic anchors and uses them to factorize aggregated mobility representations into multiple purpose-related semantic channels. It also introduces free channels to capture latent mobility patterns not covered by event data and a global channel to preserve overall spatial structure.

news.title: Poison-then-Hide: Finetuning-Activated Backdoor Attack on Pret
news.description: Backdoor attacks threaten integrity of machine learning models by allowing attackers to control model behavior through triggers. We propose Poison-then-Hide, a novel attack that remains effective when the entire model is finetuned in a domain transfer. We evaluate our method on six datasets and three model architectures, and achieve state-of-the-art (up to 97%) attack success rates.

news.title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role
news.description: Large language models trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) with verifiable rewards exhibit strong reasoning ability and broad generalization. Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) models are often viewed as more prone to memorization and limited transfer. This paper rethinks this distinction through the lens of SFT training data on widely used Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 series models.

news.title: KernelMosaic: An Open Dataset and Agentic Framework
news.description: KernelMosaic pairs diverse CUDA tasks with verified solutions and trajectories. Human-guided review and diversity-aware selection curate tasks expressed as natural-language descriptions, reference programs, mathematical specifications, and their intersections. Supervised fine-tuning of a small open-source model raises correctness from 4%, 0%, and 0% to 88%, 82%, and 16% on KernelBench L1, L2, and L3.

news.title: Nvidia has been in the midst of turmoil
news.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation has been received with worry in Israel. Many in the country are wondering how much of a reshuffle will result from the company's leadership crisis. Huang drove the company to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox for $6.9 billion in 2019. Nvidia has been responsible for a vast share of the spending in the global AI industry.

news.title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop
news.description: OpenAI launched a new wallet feature that lets its agents, called dots, help you decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on your behalf. The feature will initially be available to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, ages 18 and up, with a Visa, Mastercard, or American Express. OpenAI says users are fully in control of the purchases, as they're able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before checkout occurs.

news.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang. Megaspeed, the company led by Alice Huang, has been at the center of that trade for several years through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, and has been the subject of investigations by both the U.S. and S. government. Epoch AI estimates that about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes to hide their final destination.

news.title: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen outscores the bigger Argon
news.description: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces the Flash series, but benchmarks suggest it also makes the pricier Argon obsolete. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Hydrogen nearly matches Claude Sonnet 5.5 for less money but costs about 2.5 times more per task than GPT-6.

news.title: Anthropic Meetings lets Anthropic's AI join your video
news.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings, a feature that puts Claude into video calls as a visible participant. The feature is in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, with Google Meet as the only supported platform so far. Anthropic says more platforms will follow. Organizations running HIPAA or customer-managed encryption configurations can't use Meetings yet. All notes, transcripts, documents Claude produced are available on a dedicated page in claude.ai once the meeting ends.

news.title: Nvidia confirmed it could track chips to fight
news.description: Chip Security Act would require geotracking to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, opposed the bill and said it was 'potentially infeasible' Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the bill.

news.title: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia —
news.description: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board. Colette Kress, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President, has taken over as interim CEO. Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. She has been a regular presence on Nvidia’s earnings calls, making her a familiar figure for analysts covering the company. Her net worth is estimated to be $1.2 billion.

news.title: Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos
news.description: Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it's easier for anyone to get access to better photos. The startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop. The idea is to use AI to transform photos, whether that’s turning a group photo into a tighter portrait or transforming a selfie into a regular shot.

news.title: SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap
news.description: SoftBank announced a $7.1 billion quarterly loss on Tuesday, with over half of that stemming from losses related to power-generating equipment. SoftBank reportedly put down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed. The energy world was caught off guard by the swiftness and magnitude of AI’s rising power demands. Queues for turbine orders now extend into the early 2030s.

news.title: Jensen Huang was having a third affair, Reuters
news.description: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO and board member earlier today. CFO Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO, but no permanent successor has been named. Reuters is withholding the name of the new employee linked to Huang but says she is an employee of Nvidia. Huang has been called before Congress to testify about the national security implications of his relationship with Alice Huang.

news.title: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion
news.description: Nebius laid out $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, far more than Wall Street had expected. It rests on a string of planned projects that are already starting to show cracks. Nebius plans to fund the buildout by relying on customer pre-payments and loans backed by customer contracts. One of Nebius’ largest customers is Microsoft, which is paying for AI computing capacity at a New Jersey data center.

news.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: The unfolding Huang
news.description: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. The 63-year-old admitted Wednesday that he had three affairs, including an affair with a healthcare executive. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing.

news.title: Muse can now place calls to US businesses
news.description: Meta’s consumer AI agent Muse is now able to place calls to U.S. businesses on behalf of its users. The feature could be used to take care of calls people don’t want to make, like those to their cable company, the DMV, or to a restaurant that doesn't offer online reservations. Currently, Muse subscription plans start at $20 per month for 500 million Muse tokens.

news.title: Democrats launch investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s
news.description: Democrats open an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. The company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang earlier this week after he admitted to an affair with a Chinese spy. The alleged spy was an executive of a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia's H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States.

news.title: Australia's proposed AI safety bill would force frontier
news.description: Australia's government wants to enshrine mandatory safety rules for frontier AI companies in law. A new regulator would enforce independent model audits and impose steep penalties for violations. Canberra is deliberately prioritizing domestic regulation before entering international talks.

news.title: Google Deepmind shifts genomics AI from bulk tissue
news.description: AlphaGenome 2 identifies nearly twice as many disease-relevant gene changes as its predecessor. The model is available for noncommercial research through an API and is set to be integrated into Google's agentic platform Antigravity.

news.title: ElevenLabs Scribe v3 Live uses conversational context
news.description: Scribe v3 narrowly beats competitors like OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft on accuracy. Rivals like Microsoft and xAI run many times faster and charge roughly half the price. ElevenLabs has released two new speech recognition models.

news.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after espionage
news.description: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress is taking over on an interim basis while the board searches for a permanent successor. The move came after the Wall Street Journal reported that the board was planning to fire Huang following revelations about two extramarital affairs. Since a New York Times report on October 29 about possible ties to Chinese intelligence, Nvidia has shed roughly $1.4 trillion in market value.

news.title: Frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers
news.description: OpenAI's safety team systematically investigated why chains of thought in frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are increasingly evading oversight. Four training steps drive the erosion, including architecture choices and reinforcement learning. Loss of transparency is not law of nature but reflects tradeoffs around capability and cost.

news.title: Nine Korean startups vie for a spot
news.description: Nine early-stage South Korean startups pitch for a spot in next year's Startup Battlefield 200. Voinosis, which develops AI to detect changes in brain health through voice analysis, won the competition. The startups work across the deep tech sector, including healthcare, fintech, energy, semiconductors, and AI. All nine startups are looking to enter the U.S. market as part of the broader international expansion plans.

news.title: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access
news.description: Cyberattack at Fireworks AI has exposed some of its customers’ data, the company has confirmed. Hackers gained access to a Fireworks development system, which allowed access to some of the company's customers' data. At least one confirmed affected customer is online document editor and notetaker Notion, which said the breach affected around 1% of its own customers. This is the second breach affecting Fireworks in as many months, following a security incident in October.

news.title: Norwest pushes deeper into AI with new $4B
news.description: Norwest, backed solely by Wells Fargo, has raised a $4 billion fund as it sets out to invest more in AI. This is the eighteenth fund for the 65-year-old multi-stage investment firm, and its largest to date. The fund will be invested across various sectors and multiple countries, notably the United States, India, and Israel. Norwest said Thursday it aims to capitalize on AI startups developing products and services across core industries.

news.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen
news.description: President Donald Trump says former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday. In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place. Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Cook stepped down as Apple CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is bad enough. He chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation. Huang has been the biggest, loudest advocate for open-weight AI models in the tech industry and among government policymakers. Huang's influence has been lost right when he was using it to push tech industry in a number of directions.

news.title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights
news.description: United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf. The airline is the latest American corporate giant to prevent customers from using AI agents and autonomous assistants to access their systems. The move comes as airlines and banks are struggling to differentiate between real customers and AI systems operating on their behalf, such as when users share their logins with their AI assistants.

news.title: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting
news.description: Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue briefly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday, calling it a “really sad day” Nvidia had announced its plan to acquire the platform for open-source AI models in September for $12.9 billion. The U.S. Department of Justice began making inquiries about how the deal would impact competition in the AI market.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia's support for open
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. Huang’s exit raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community. Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running AI systems.

news.title: Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator
news.description: Nectar is an AI-powered operating system for marketing. Its new “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform. Nectar says its Creator Agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction.

news.title: Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers
news.description: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The Gemini 4 Hydrogen model is designed for fast execution across agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than its previous fast model, Gemini 3.8 Flash.

news.title: Google joins decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1
news.description: Google Deepmind's Gemini Decisions API evaluates up to 1,000 closed-ended questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, and video. Gemini Decision 1 returns results in 150 to 250 milliseconds at roughly five times lower cost than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.

news.title: Databricks’ new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi
news.description: Databricks unveils updated version of its AI agent Genie, which can now perform multistep jobs that take extended work to finish. CEO Ali Ghodsi showed me how he uses Genie internally and how it analyzed employee satisfaction surveys. He says Genie can do for the business side what AI, agents, and harnesses are doing for programmers. Genie can also be used in personal life, rather than a security-questionable alternative like OpenClaw or Instinct.

news.title: With $720M round, Fractile gets a leg up
news.description: British startup Fractile raises $720 million Series C for purpose-built AI chips. The company is one of the top-funded startups in the race to build AI chips in the U.K. The new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year” According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” - quite possibly $7 billion.

news.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts
news.description: CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices. The company reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense.

news.title: How backlash and red tape continue to slow
news.description: The data center boom is running into serious real-world obstacles, from widespread local opposition and permitting delays to scramble for electricity. A lot of the projects being announced may never get built in the first place. With billions of dollars in AI infrastructure investment at stake, separating realistic projects from speculative ones is becoming increasingly important. On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, hosts Rebecca Bellan and Tim De Chant are joined by Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy at Ascend Analytics.

news.title: The data center you dread might never even
news.description: The data center boom is running into serious real-world obstacles, from widespread local opposition and permitting delays to scramble for electricity. A lot of the projects being announced may never get built in the first place. With billions of dollars in AI infrastructure investment at stake, separating realistic projects from speculative ones is becoming increasingly important. On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, hosts Rebecca Bellan and Tim De Chant are joined by Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy at Ascend Analytics.

news.title: Jensen Huang accused of having another affair —
news.description: The New York Times reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is suspected of having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. The Times says it was told of the alleged affair by five employees at the company. Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles. The Wall Street Journal reports that the Nvidia board is preparing to oust Huang.

news.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps
news.description: Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years. Sources say the board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang's future at the company. On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman purported by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday.

news.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: The unfolding Huang
news.description: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond his personal life and potentially impact national security. U.S. officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. The Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with a company vice president of health care, who reports directly to him.

news.title: A highly unscientific list of possible successors
news.description: It's almost inconceivable that Nvidia would fire its rock star CEO Jensen Huang. Even if Huang is pushed out as CEO, the board members he has made very rich are unlikely to cut him loose entirely. But someone still has to run the company, and there’s no apparent succession plan, which leaves us speculating while we wait to see what happens next.

news.title: OpenAI turns ChatGPT into a business directory
news.description: OpenAI turns ChatGPT into a business directory with AI agents that handle customer questions. "Business Agents" let eligible US e-commerce providers talk to customers directly inside ChatGpt. Companies can claim their profile, add product data, and track how users interact with them. The "Business Agent" will handle questions from US retailers directly in chatGPT's new Business Hub, which is open to US customers.

news.title: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they
news.description: England's higher education regulator says AI has made it "nearly impossible" to fairly assess student coursework. Investigation found that students are having ChatGPT write entire papers undetected, without being able to recall basic content afterward. To save the credibility of degrees, universities now have to return to traditional exams or face sanctions. UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats or adopt traditional exam formats.

news.title: Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10
news.description: OpenAI grew its quarterly revenue 50 percent to $10 billion but is still burning more cash than it brings in. Rival Anthropic operates far more efficiently on $17 billion in revenue. To close the gap, OpenAI is now fueling a price war for enterprise customers. OpenAI still trails Anthropic, which operates on more than $17 million in revenue, by $10.9 billion in 2013. The company's quarterly revenue grew 50 percent but still burned more cash.

news.title: US data brokers are selling half a billion
news.description: US data brokers like Mercor, Surge AI, and AfterQuery are selling roughly half a billion dollars' worth of AI training data to Chinese labs. That includes the same RL environments previously built for OpenAI or Anthropic. At least nine firms are involved, and export controls barely apply, according to a ChinaTalk investigation. The report says that at least nine companies are involved in selling the data to the labs.

news.title: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia's CUDA lead
news.description: Anthropic claims it used AI itself to breach Nvidia's CUDA moat. Anthropic's in-house model Mythos reportedly ported Claude to AMD GPUs in just three days. Animations now run Claude on four chip families and aims to cut costs and reduce vendor dependencies. Anthropics now runs Claude on a range of chip families, with almost no human intervention. Company hopes to reduce vendor dependency and cut costs by cutting costs.

news.title: Helsing built an AI system that prepares targets
news.description: Helsing has unveiled Clarity, an AI platform that uses agents to distill sensor data into target recommendations for weapons systems. All under human oversight and European control. But experience from the Iran war, Gaza, and near-miss involving China shows that the speed of automation and data fusion create risks that are hard to contain. Helsing says every decision will carry a human name and the AI platform will be under European oversight.

news.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code verified Signal's cryptographic core
news.description: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code mathematically verified Signal's cryptographic core code in four weeks instead of years. AI agents powered by Gemini Carbon wrote more than six million lines of proof code and flagged only about one percent for human review. Deepmind plans to extend the method to critical infrastructure like power grids and medical devices like medical devices. The algorithm was developed by Google's Deepmind and Gemini Carbon, the company behind Gemini Carbon.

news.title: US corporate AI spending hits a new high
news.description: According to the Ramp AI Index, US corporate AI spending rose just 1.65 percent in October 2026. One percent of companies still drive 80 percent of revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. Customer support is emerging as a new growth driver, but it may bring lower margins than the coding business that has fueled spending so far. US spending hits a new high in October, but growth slows to 1.66 percent.

news.title: Tabular Foundation Models in Financial Predictions are based
news.description: TabFM is more accurate than all comparison models. It is faster and less computationally intensive than the large language model. Several tree-based specifications produce predictions more quickly than TabFM, so choosing between them involves a trade-off between accuracy and speed. We conclude that TFMs have promise as a new tool for forecasting in accounting and finance. However, our evaluation is based on a single benchmark task, and no class of models will dominate in all settings.

news.title: Deep Personalization: Continuous Context Observation for Local Proactive
news.description: Proactive agents hold the promise to close this gap, but effective proactivity requires understanding users' real-time activities and personalizing intervention timing. We introduce deep personalization in Coco, a proactive desktop agent, by having a separate Observer Agent that monitors desktop activity, maintains compact long-term user modeling context, and learns when assistance is desirable from implicit signals such as engagement, dismissal, explicit requests, and repeated work patterns. Coco improves its macro-averaged F1 score from 0.199 to 0.515, a 2.4-3.0x relative gain.

news.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons
news.description: Radical Numerics has developed a model that it says can identify natural and AI-engineered pathogens without an internet connection. Many scientists say AI-made bioweapons are a low-likelihood threat. The company hopes its technology will help researchers and public health officials identify emerging biological threats. In one experiment, the company removed Bundibugyo virus—which is currently driving an Ebola outbreak in East Africa—from the training data.

news.title: Nvidia's crisis has corporate governance experts reaching
news.description: Nvidia’s stock sank 5.47% on Tuesday, following a 4% drop on Monday, a loss of about 9.5% in two days. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. Two corporate governance professors say there is no real precedent for a CEO caught up in a suspected honeypot.

news.title: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better
news.description: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads. Co-founders Ilan Kadar and Elad Levi previously worked for Nexar, which develops autonomous driving technology. On Wednesday, the startup said it had raised $13 million in seed funding to make that happen. The platform works alongside existing agentic tools like Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and Cursor.

news.title: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B
news.description: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time. That would mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year. The company's profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109%. OpenAI has now reached an annual revenue run rate of $50B, according to Bloomberg.

news.title: Congress to call Jensen Huang in to answer
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has until the end of the day to respond to a congressional request to answer questions about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House Republicans have asked Huang to appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing in regards to his relations with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang. House China committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.

news.title: You Don't Need Feature Learning to Do
news.description: We study how rotation-invariant kernel machines learn the ICL linear regression task proposed by Raventos et al. (2023) The generalizing solution is approximately a low-degree truncation of the memorizing solution, and so the model first generalizes, then degrades into memorization as training proceeds. The fact that kernel machines can generalize on this task means that feature learning is inessential to ICL.

news.title: Free Lunch Uncertainty: Sequence-Level R\'enyi Entropy from Part
news.description: Quantifying uncertainty over an entire LLM completion is critical for selective prediction and adaptive compute. We show that Sequential Monte Carlo decoding for power sampling already estimates the normalizing constant of the power distribution. We prove that orders above one are tied to the most likely token of each step, which explains why they track log-probability, while the order-1/2 member accumulates the log of per-step search effort. This member is the best zero-cost selective-prediction signal in 10 of 13 settings.

news.title: Looping Deeper Without Growing the KV Cache: Recurrent
news.description: Looped language models deepen computation without adding parameters, yet caching full-context key-value (KV) states across layers and rounds severely bounds serving batch size. We design a looped causal encoder-decoder (CED) that achieves recurrent depth with zero round-wise KV growth. We find that recurrence must be placed in the encoder to iteratively refine global KV representations rather than re-reading static decoder projections.

news.title: Reconstructing Boundary Layer Wind Profiles with Machine Learning
news.description: Wind profiles in the atmospheric boundary layer drive short-range forecasting and wind-energy siting. We benchmark modern tabular learners against analytical parameterizations on 158,097 IGRA soundings. CatBoost, TabM, and FT-Transformer reduce RMSE to 1.3-1.6 m/s. Once the predictor set is fixed the three architectures differ by less than 0.05 m/S, so accuracy is driven by predictors rather than architecture.

news.title: Intent: Out-of-Sample, Cold-Start Evaluation on User Event Sequ
news.description: Banks now train foundation models on ordered sequences of customer events such as transactions, app sessions, and authorizations. The most common defect is the lack of a calendar timestamp that orders events. We present INTENT (INTEraction, Novelty, and Transfer evaluation for next-action prediction), a public benchmark that scores a model in seven cells defined by whether the user, the period, and the target item appeared in training.

news.title: Permutation-Based Pre-trained Model Merging via Reciprocal Orthog
news.description: (2026) showed that sufficiently wide, independently trained neural networks can exhibit linear mode connectivity (LMC) with softmax temperature calibration. LMC means that a low-loss linear path connects the models' parameters. This behavior is explained by layerwise exponentially weighted connectivity (LEWC), whereby each merged layer outputs an exponentially weighted sum of the original models' corresponding representations, yielding ensemble-like predictions. We therefore search for permutations that encourage reciprocal orthogonality (RO), which suppresses interference between each model's weights and the other model's representations.

news.title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic
news.description: Linear probes are a standard method to study geometric structures, such as helices and circles, from the activations of large language models. Such structure is often taken as evidence that the model computes with it. We propose that probe results be reported as verdicts on all four claims rather than as a single accuracy. We apply the pipeline to two-digit addition and multiplication in GPT-J 6B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Pythia 6.9B.

news.title: Multimodal Graph Learning: A Survey of Models, Benchmarks
news.description: Multimodal attributed graphs (MAGs) underlie e-commerce, social media, content platforms, and creative applications. Learning on MAGs has developed along two complementary lines: graph-centric methods redesign how modalities are fused, propagated, and connected within message passing. In parallel, several benchmarks have appeared with different datasets and evaluation protocols. This survey takes an algorithm-centric and evaluation-grounded view of the field.

news.title: Ring, known for its doorbell cameras, launches home
news.description: Ring, known for its doorbell cameras, launches a home security drone and an enterprise security robot. Ring Drone Cam is designed to fly from room to room, inspecting what is happening in a user's house and, if there's trouble, to alert them. Ring Rover Cam is a roving enterprise security bot, designed for businesses. Both devices are powered by the same proprietary AI system, known as AI Pilot.

news.title: Spotify's AI DJ gets new voices, personalities
news.description: Spotify's AI DJ gets new voices, personalities, and an option for less chatter. Users can now choose from an expanded set of AI DJ voices in both English and Spanish. The new voices begin rolling out today, November 10, to Premium users in the markets where DJ is already supported. The other change allows users to toggle off the commentary between songs, reducing the DJ's interruptions. Spotify says the DJ is used by over 94 million Spotify Premium listeners.

news.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond his personal life and potentially impact national security. U.S. officials believe that Huang's likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. As an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to China.

news.title: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel
news.description: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M. Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Oura also announced that its revenue grew 153% year-over-year to $533 million for the quarter ended on September 30. Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, alongside the company’s 70 employees.

news.title: Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M
news.description: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO. Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share. Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million worth of shares through his donor-advised fund. The seven founders will own about 3.2% of the total outstanding Class A shares, the S-1 says. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of votes.

news.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s
news.description: The RAISE Act, New York's AI safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. Large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027. Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations. Governor Kathy Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research.

news.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder
news.description: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder Julie Bort. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. The AI lab has not announced new travel-specific products or plans. Travel is also one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. OpenAI's ChatGPT agent mentioned travel as one of its potential uses in July 2025.

news.title: Anthropic kicks off IPO roadshow, offering shares
news.description: Anthropic is kicking off its IPO roadshow, targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion. The company is securing $26 billion through a private placement with Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, and other major tech firms as anchor investors. The IPO comes at a time when investors are growing increasingly skeptical of AI investments. It is expected to fetch $64.4 billion in the public offering of shares at $70 to $78.

news.title: Eight countries and top AI labs agree
news.description: Eight countries along with representatives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Mistral AI have signed the "Paris Call for AI Safety and Security" at Emmanuel Macron's initiative. The companies commit to shutdown mechanisms, independent audits, and disclosing known risks, but the agreement lacks binding sanctions or deadlines. The agreement does not have binding deadlines or binding sanctions, but it does not include a deadline or a binding deadline.

news.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 scores 96 percent
news.description: Google Deepmind introduces Gemini Robotics 2.5, a new control model for robots. Apollo 2 sorted metal parts on active Mercedes-Benz production lines in Hungary and Germany. The robot Apollo 2 had a reported success rate of 96 percent sorting metal parts in the pilot pilot. The humanoid robot was tested with Apptronik and Google DeepMind's Apollo 2 robot with a reported 96 percent success rate in sorting parts.

news.title: Gemini 4 Carbon arrives just in time
news.description: Google is making Gemini 4 Carbon generally available after a two-week testing phase. The model ranks first in several benchmarks, in some cases ahead of Anthropic's new Fable 5.2, at less than half the per-task cost. Google is also previewing coordinated agent teams through the "/swarm" feature, which split up complex tasks in real time. The new model arrives just in time to feel like yesterday's news in the fastest model cycle yet.

news.title: Nvidia's model GR00T 2 watches humans on video
news.description: Nvidia's new AI model GR00T 2 is designed to teach robots new tasks without laborious teleoperation. Success rates still vary widely, though, ranging from 10 to 80 percent depending on the task. System transfers human hand movements from videos to robotic arms, trained on about 400,000 hours of video footage. Success rate varies widely, but it's up to 80 per cent depending on what task needs to be done.

news.title: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+
news.description: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+ languages. The company is also adding support for 27 languages, its largest language expansion to date. Once the rollout is complete, Otter will support 31 languages, making the platform more accessible to international teams. The announcement comes as Otter continues to expand beyond transcription and into other workplace AI tools, following its $320 million funding from General Catalyst. It recently introduced Work Mode, which uses meeting history and connected apps to help users prepare for upcoming calls.

news.title: Cyberattacks threaten to make open source
news.description: Hugging Face CEO Irene Solaiman says open AI platforms are vulnerable to cyberattacks. She says open doors and rich data make them vulnerable to attacks. The October attack on OpenCode, which targeted users’ third-party API keys, is the latest example. The risks aren’t limited to platforms that invite open community contributions. Solaiman: There’s a “danger of open source really closing down at a time when we’ve gotten so much public support”.

news.title: Cyanogen's co-founder takes aim at Windows
news.description: After challenging Google's Android with Cyanogen, its co-founder takes aim at Windows for AI era. Kora Systems is developing a Linux-based desktop operating system that integrates AI models and agents directly into the computing experience. The software is expected to launch in 2027 as a free-to-use desktop system. Microsoft has long dominated the PC operating-system market, making it hard for newer players to establish a foothold.

news.title: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70
news.description: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share to reach an implied valuation of $1.404 trillion. The company could end up being worth a hefty $1 trillion if its shares list at the top of the price range, on a fully diluted basis. Anthropic intends to start trading on the Nasdaq close to November 19, per reporting from CNBC, under the ticker symbol "ANT" The company said its run-rate revenue reached $81 billion by the end of October.

news.title: Adobe brings AI agents and new creative tools
news.description: Adobe brings AI agents and new creative tools to Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly. The company is also releasing a Model Context Protocol (MCP) that lets other chatbots use Adobe features. Adobe's Firefly app is moving into Figma's territory with a new prototyping tool in private beta called Builder. Adobe is also making it easier for people to take quick action, like removing the background or generating a thumbnail for a video.

news.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch
news.description: Meta's AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS. Users can now interact with the AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation directly on their smartwatch. The smartwatch launch comes just a month after Meta introduced a dedicated iPad app for Muse. Last week, Meta rolled out the ability for users in the U.S. to video chat with their Muse AI avatar. The AI agent doesn't actually see users, but can hear them and respond in real time.

news.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two
news.description: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips. The new units are part of the company's eighth generation of chips introduced in April this year. The launch comes as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and even AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are working on their own lines of AI-specific semiconductors and accompanying software. The news comes at a particularly vulnerable moment for Nvidia, whose CEO admitted to having an affair with a Chinese spy.

news.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions
news.description: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks. Anthropic also unveils Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets. The company also announced Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The launch of Anthropic's new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to visualize company information and create presentations.

news.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT
news.description: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google. Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products. The Business Hub will also give users access to limited business insights, including profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other metrics. The feature is currently in beta.

news.title: PSI is trying to make a business out
news.description: Physical Superintelligence (PSI) is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery. The startup is focused on understanding how to take computational results and validate them with experiments. The long play is converting theoretical physics breakthroughs into actual technologies. PSI CEO Matt Pines: "At the end of the day, physics is different than math because it's the real world because nature gets a vote in your models of reality".

news.title: These Robotic Arms are Powered by Algae
news.description: Soft, flexible robots could be useful for a wide variety of applications, including artificial muscles and wearable devices. Researchers at Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands have developed a soft robotic arm colonized by algae on its surface. The key to the movement of these flexible robots is the algae’s photosynthetic capabilities. The tiny robot arms are constructed of two layers of hydrogel that the algae cells live on.

news.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company's efforts to loosen chip export restrictions. The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia, which has been a big market for the company in China. Even if Nvidia's investigation finds that Huang didn’t share secrets with his paramour, the question is whether he’ll be able to convince Washington that Nvidia can still do business with China.

news.title: The race is on to sue Nvidia
news.description: Law professor: "I would definitely wager that there’ll be a filing" A new lawsuit accuses Nvidia of misleading investors about its CEO's ties to a data center executive. Law expert: Nvidia's CEO's knowledge gets imputed to the company. Lawyer: Nvidia misled investors because CEO Jensen Huang was having an affair with a top exec. Nvidia's stock slid more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after board said it would investigate CEO.

news.title: A short seller flagged Nvidia CEO’s ties
news.description: A short seller flagged Nvidia CEO's ties to a suspected Chinese spy six months before the scandal. U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang and influence his position on advanced AI chips. The Nvidia CEO admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend and the company has now opened a formal investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang. The short seller firm Culper Research had already raised questions about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's unusually close relationship with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that buys Nvidia chips.

news.title: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO
news.description: Anthropic plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week. Investors will look to Anthropic’s valuation to gauge the strength of the AI boom. Some institutional investors are now pushing for a valuation below the $1.5 trillion target discussed as recently as last week. OpenAI's main rival, ChatGPT, was reportedly valued at $1 billion last week after raising $11 billion in fresh capital.

news.title: Nvidia espionage scandal weakens Huang's lobby against tighter
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman US intelligence agencies classify as a suspected Chinese informant. The affair weakens Huang's lobbying efforts against stricter AI chip export controls. Newly elected Democratic Congress is poised to ramp up scrutiny of AI chip smuggling to China and push for tighter restrictions. The board has launched an independent investigation into the affair and the affair has been described as 'an affair'.

news.title: Google ships four TPU variants in one year
news.description: Google ships four TPU variants in one year as it ramps up competition with Nvidia. Google is increasingly positioning its in-house chips as an alternative to Nvidia's. The TPU 8i Max doubles compute power and memory by placing two chips on a single package. With nearly 100 external customers now on board, Google is positioning its TPU chips as alternative to the Nvidia's GPUs. The company has also added two specialized variants: the TPU8tx keeps sensitive data encrypted even during processing.

news.title: Tencent's AI chief says AI bioweapons are coming
news.description: Tencent chief AI scientist Vinces Yao Shunyu warns that AI will soon be able to develop bioweapons. While safety filters on open-source systems can be easily stripped through abliteration, closed models like Anthropic's Claude often block too aggressively. For its upcoming open-weight model Hy4, Tencent is filtering dangerous hacking knowledge directly from the training data. Tencent's Hy4 will be an open-weights model for its upcoming model.

news.title: Disney bets on Adobe's Firefly to create brand-safe
news.description: Disney and Adobe are building custom AI tools together for the entertainment giant's productions. The multi-year partnership was announced at Adobe's MAX conference. Disney gets early access to new Adobe technology for its theme parks, cruise line, and ESPN content. Adobe says it will use Adobe Firefly Foundry to build custom models tailored to Disney's brands. Disney had previously struck a deal with OpenAI and walked away from it, and was involved in the bankruptcy of Character.AI.

news.title: Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100
news.description: Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable editing across 100 rounds without color drift. It generates native RGBA images with transparent backgrounds. Bytedance Seed outperforms GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst in realism. A Pro version is planned for the next version of the image model, Seedream is available now. It supports stable multi-pass editing over up to 100 iterations, says Seedance Seed.

news.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a small AI model
news.description: Meta is introducing Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient AI model. It delivers more intelligence per dollar than Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna. But it falls short when it comes to actual programming tasks such as tool calls, routing, and data extraction. The model is optimized for repetitive agent tasks like tool calls and routing, such as data extraction, says Meta. The Decoder.com.

news.title: Anthropic 5.2 and Mythos 5. 2 cement Anthropic's
news.description: Anthropic is releasing Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5. 2 in two versions: one freely available and one reserved for verified organizations. Anthropic says it has deliberately curbed any capabilities that would let the AI accelerate its own development. The models solve open physics problems, show stronger cybersecurity capabilities, design functioning operating systems, and write more than 90 percent of the changes merged into Anthropic's core code.

news.title: Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry
news.description: Connected data, AI, and advanced modeling are helping scientists accelerate research and develop more sustainable materials. The challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions. The opportunity lies in bringing these capabilities together responsibly and at scale, says Girish Rao.

news.title: Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate
news.description: Scott Wiener has made AI regulation a cornerstone of his political career. As a California state senator, Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Wiener’s congressional campaign received over $3 million from a nonprofit in favor of AI regulation that receives substantial funding from Anthropic. “We need to slow this down, and we could sleepwalk into a disaster," Wiener says.

news.title: The backlash about data centers might really just
news.description: The real fault line is electricity: drawing it from the grid and generating it onsite provoke different kinds of backlash. The average data center operating in this part of Virginia today has a power capacity of 54 megawatts. That’s more than the power draw of the Denver International Airport. Data center developers told me they’re preparing for new rules that would cut them off from grid power during peak demand. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the physical consequences of its appetite for electricity.

news.title: Language Model Deployment on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices
news.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed many areas of artificial intelligence (AI) but their substantial resource requirements limit their deployment on mobile and edge devices. Edge deployment offers benefits including local data processing, cost savings, reduced latency, and personalized responses. This paper reviews the latest techniques that make the deployment of LLMs on edge devices feasible. arXiv:2611.09075v1 Announcement: The next challenge is deploying these models on resource-limited edge devices.

news.title: Medium’s new TK app brings AI assistance directly
news.description: 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Medium's new TK app brings AI assistance directly into the writing process. TK aims to bring AI technology deeper into writing process by incorporating an AI assistant into the idea behind TKK. Medium launched a new app on Monday allowing users to ask for help by typing "@TK".

news.description: 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Anthropic buys $3.4 billion worth of natural gas turbines for $3 billion. Anthropics joins $3B frenzy, buys $4B worth of $7.7 billion in natural gas. TechCrunch has become so acute that power crunch crunch has become acute that Anthropic is spending up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity.

news.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid
news.description: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. The company says the new models “show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision” and communicate more clearly with users. Notably, Anthropic is lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. As a result, Fable 5.2 is now cheaper than its primary competitor GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic says that the new version of Fable will return responses 30% faster across.

news.title: Jensen Huang pulls out of 11Labs Summit amid
news.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pulled out of the ElevenLabs Summit scheduled for this week. Huang admitted to an extarital affair over the weekend with a possible Chinese spy. Huang: "I owe all of you an apology I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt my children and there is no excuse for what happened".

news.title: LLM Persona Simulation: Signal Form in Cold-Start E-Commerce
news.description: Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential alternative by simulating persona-conditioned user responses. Using real Google Ads e-commerce campaign data across five demographic segments, we identify three signal-form dimensions that affect simulation quality. Systematic ablations show that minimal demographic descriptions achieve lower mean error than richer persona configurations. Relative qualitative cues substantially outperform the tested quantitative anchors. We additionally compare these configurations with direct-prior and rule-based baselines and with alternative LLM configurations.

news.title: MotionBench-XAI: Benchmarking What Shapes Shapley Explanations
news.description: MotionBench-XAI is a benchmark built on five synthetic spatiotemporal datasets with exact ground-truth Shapley values. We show that grouping features into players, across time, space, or both, matters more than the choice of imputer. Generative imputers improve explanations only when their conditional models are accurate. We distill these findings into practical insights and provide an open-source pipeline to provide practical insights.

news.title: TopoSHAP: Shapley for Explainable and Efficient Topological Deep
news.description: TopoSHAP-cell assigns Shapley values to topological data cells and extracts compact explanations. These explanations match or outperform graph-based counterparts on GraphXAI benchmark data. They also reveal advantageous topological feature design, leading to measured improvements in explanation recovery and predictive accuracy. This is up to $11.3\times$ cheaper than traditional TDL training sweeps. arXiv:2611.08789v1.

news.title: On Lipschitz Explosion in Deep Neural Networks
news.description: The Lipschitz constant of a neural network is a basic stability quantity appearing in optimization guarantees, generalization bounds, and robustness certificates. We prove that, for deep networks with normalization layers, both can grow exponentially with depth and hence with parameter dimension. The theory predicts that perturbations introducing new singular directions should be amplified much more strongly than those at the same noise level that remain within the input's original singular subspace. The latter also yields a concrete rank separation mechanism for adversarial vulnerability.

news.title: Patching the Blind Spots: Reversible LLM Rule Overlay
news.description: We propose a framework that patches such a model without modifying it: LLMs propose rules anchored on features the model underweights by SHAP. The resulting noisy pool is screened for empirical support and calibrated into an additive, reversible log-lift overlay that runs at the production cut-off. On a real-world e-commerce fraud detector trained on selection-biased data, continued training regresses even when carefully tuned.

news.title: Dual-Stream LLM-Guided Reward Design for Reject-Inference
news.description: Production fraud-detection models learn from a censored slice of their own traffic: transactions a legacy system blocked never receive fraud labels. We extend LLM-guided reward design, the framework of Qu et al. (2025) in which an LLM evolves the reward of a two-step REINFORCE fraud-blocking policy, to attack this reject-inference problem inside the reward. We expose superset of evidence and let the LLM decide for itself which to use.

news.title: Foundation-Model Residuals as Signals of Urban Bus Irregularity
news.description: Pretrained trajectory models encode mobility patterns learned across cities, but their errors when transferred to a new city are usually treated only as performance limitations. We instead ask whether these residuals reveal systematic local conditions. Insights into such varied environments are increasingly valuable for evaluating new urban paradigms, such as 15-minute-city perspective, guide our approach. We interpret high residuals as candidate proxy signals of transit irregularity rather than direct evidence of service disruption.

news.title: Higher Order Component Attribution via Learned Surrogates
news.description: Experimental High Energy Physics (HEP) has adopted the transformer architecture for identification of jets, particularly the state-of-the-art Particle Transformer (ParT) which injects explicit information about particle correlations into the attention mechanism. We propose component attribution methods using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) that directly tie back to the physical descriptors of jets. We hope to probe whether mechanisms such as Multi-Head Attention (MHA), or the ParT architecture, are able to learn these as discriminating features.

news.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Chaotic Three-Body Dynamics
news.description: Machine learning (ML) and generative AI have recently made impressive progress in understanding physics. We explore a hierarchy of prediction problems stemming from chaotic three-body systems and benchmark existing ML approaches. We benchmark a range of ML approaches, from simple regression methods to state-of-the-art physics models, across these tasks. Code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/Simonwan03/ThreeBodyMLBench.

news.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural
news.description: The Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) literature has produced a rapidly expanding catalogue of methods. We propose a new evaluation protocol that treats the four components as an integrated system. We release PINNpipe, an innovative JAX package containing 18 different methods from the current literature as well as nine efficiently implemented benchmark problems. We illustrate our evaluation protocol in relation to established benchmark studies and report results that challenge common assumptions.

news.title: LLM Agents are learning on Low-Budget Molecular Optimization
news.description: On PMO at 50 oracle calls, a GPT-4o mini agent's sum AUC falls from 14.44 to 4.85 after task names and curated reference compounds are hidden. Identity-blinded condition that states only the oracle form (e.g., similarity to a hidden reference) scores 5.39, while a deterministic retrieval-only baseline with no LLM reaches 12.16 (84% of the full agent) This summary.

news.title: Interpretable Multifidelity Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
news.description: Multifidelity surrogate modeling addresses this problem by combining inexpensive low-fidelity data with limited high fidelity data. MFKAN performs comparably to MFNN for one-time-step-forward prediction while also providing closed-form symbolic equations unavailable with MFNN. KAN and FNN achieve comparable self-evaluation accuracy (Pearson correlation of roughly 0.73--0.81), but both perform poorly at true cross-f fidelity forecasting.

news.title: Does Country Matter? Evaluating Geographic Sensitivity of Large
news.description: Large language models (LLMs) show strong zero-shot reasoning capabilities, yet their sensitivity to prompt context raises questions about reliability in deployment. Study investigates whether geographic context embedded in prompts influences LLM-based chronic kidney disease (CKD) screening, independent of any change in patient features. Findings demonstrate that geographic tokens can systematically shift clinical screening outcomes despite identical patient inputs, with implications for the deployment of LLM decision support in diverse healthcare settings.

news.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship
news.description: Nvidia will investigate possible relationship with possible Chinese spy Anthony Huang’s relationship with Chinese PM Anthony Ha Ha. Nvidia also announced Sunday that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation. Nvidia also published a message that Huang sent to the company admitting he had an affair with a former executive at Singapore chip company Megaspeed.

news.title: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it’s “about a 50
news.description: Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang told staff he was unfaithful to his wife. But this isn’t a case of just another CEO having an extramarital affair. The romantic interest is Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy who was feeding information back to Beijing. In short, the stakes reach well beyond Nvidia, given how many tech and financial partners depend on its place at the center of the AI economy.

news.title: AI coding agents still need human cleanup
news.description: Alibaba's new coding-agent benchmark, Co-Design Bench, tests AI agents on real user requests that already tripped them up in practice. Even GPT-6 Astra, the top performer, fully solves only 26.4 percent of tasks. On older benchmarks, the same models score above 99 percent on older benchmarks. The new benchmark tests the best coding agents on a range of real-world tasks.

news.title: The inventor of the bitter lesson has
news.description: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton reaffirms that raw compute alone isn't enough for intelligence and that fundamentally new learning methods are needed. Ex-OpenAI researcher Tworek agrees, saying blind transformer scaling "has reward hacked brains of a whole generation of scientists" A growing wave of startups is already betting on exactly this gap. The inventor of the bitter lesson has a bitter lesson for LLM scaling enthusiasts, he says.

news.title: The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may
news.description: Consciousness researchers Anil Seth, Ned Block, and Giulio Tononi argue in a Nature commentary that today's AI systems aren't conscious and won't become so on silicon hardware. They consider the assumption that consciousness depends on computation alone "fatally flawed" and warn against granting rights to AI systems. The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate, the researchers say.

news.title: Andrej Karpathy built a curated video platform
news.description: Andrej Karpathy, OpenAI co-founder and current Anthropic AI researcher, built HackerTube over a weekend. Claude filtered 43 million comments from 20 years of Hacker News and distilled them into 6,454 videos. The result is a "significantly better viewing experience" than YouTube's own recommendations. The site needs no login, shows a single mid-video frame instead of optimized thumbnails, and stores state locally in the browser.

news.title: Megaspeed exec recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO
news.description: A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. news.title: Two-stage residual learning for calibrated uncertainty in solar
news.description: Machine learning models are increasingly used to predict solar output, but they typically report a single value and capture the associated uncertainty poorly. We develop an alternative two-stage method, motivated by synthetic solar signal generation, in which the forecast error is modeled separately from the expected irradiance. We show that explicitly modeling the error brings the predicted standard deviation markedly closer to the historical value, reducing the deviation between the two by 34.6 percent and by 56.5 percent when the LSTM is coupled to Gaussian process regression.

news.title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations are fingerprints
news.description: Symmetry governs organization of physical structures, while symmetry breaking reveals their transformations. In geometric deep learning, symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations, limiting the expressive capacity of graph neural networks. We introduce spectral symmetry fingerprints (SymFP), which enable discrete point-group identification through rank-template matching and continuous symmetry analysis. SymFP is orientation invariant and architecture agnostic, enabling a parameter-free GNN implementation. Its spectra can be reused across multiple target groups and the resulting leakage scores satisfy subgroup monotonicity.

news.title: Using Transformers for Teaching and Learning via Symbolic
news.description: Distilling neural networks into compact symbolic policies can help humans understand agent behavior in A-life. Such networks are generally opaque to a human observer. Distilling a neural policy into a symbolic policy is typically performed by searching the space of symbolic policies to find one that approximates the neural policy. The space of policies can be large, necessitating incomplete stochastic search such as genetic algorithms. We propose to instead use a transformer pre-trained on readily available random percept-action data.

news.title: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models
news.description: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) are vulnerable to compositional harm. Images and prompts that are benign in isolation become harmful through the model's cross-modal reasoning. news.title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology
news.description: We present a scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification (GPC) framework that operates on frozen pathology foundation model embeddings (Phikon) We evaluate on two histopathology benchmarks for breast cancer metastasis detection: PCam and CAMELYON17-WILDS. news.title: A Night at the LLM Zoo: Data Conditioned
news.description: A challenge to Weight Space Learning as it expands from task specific and vision models to Large Language Models is the absence of a well curated and analyzed LLM population. We show that the zoo contains diverse models whose variation is structured by training mixture composition. We embed the data mixture composition to condition a Flow Matching model of complete pretrained LLM weights in Gram-PCA compressed weight space. Finally, we produce all source code and artifacts to support the continued expansion of the LLM domain.

news.title: Stochastic Dynamics of Generative AI: From Autoregressive Models
news.description: This paper develops a stochastic dynamical-systems perspective on three classes of generative AI models. We formulate large language models (LLMs) as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models with attention-based dependencies. We consider networks of interacting LLMs and characterize their collective behavior through mean-field ordinary differential equations. These dynamics provide a framework for understanding emergent preferential attachment and persistent structural biases, including type-dependent glass-ceiling effects.

news.title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi

news.description: Using a canonical behavioural task and modelling with neural networks, we develop and test a theory for why simple-to-complex curricula succeed. news.title: One Mistake, Three Layers: Persistence Rules Under Depth

news.title: DeepSeek indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in deepSeek

news.description: Understanding the training dynamics of deep neural networks in large-scale limits is a question both of foundational and of practical importance. news.title: Localizing predictive concepts encoded in neural representations via
news.description: Understanding which regulatory sequence motifs a genomic deep learning model has learned is essential for trusting its use in downstream tasks such as variant effect prediction. news.title: Characterizing Recoverable Expert-Utilization Signatures in Fine-Tuned M
news.description: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models are increasingly deployed in distributed environments, from federated learning to edge-cloud systems. We uncover structural memorization: a novel vulnerability where a fine-tuned model memorizes not only its training data but also its internal pathway used to process it, creating a characteristic routing fingerprint unique to the training process. We show that these memorized expert pathways can be stealthily recovered through the model's unconditional generation, using only routing and output logits.

news.title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token
news.description: There exists little mathematical theory explaining why Transformer architectures are empirically successful even for non-Markovian data. This paper studies next-token prediction via stochastic optimal control theoretically trained Transformers for such sources. For stationary ergodic sources, the resulting error is bounded by an entropy gap; for $N$th order Markovian sources, it decays at an exponential rate. We then construct a Transformer of depth $M+1$ one head per layer, realizing the truncated filter, and we optimally train it with stochastically control developed in earlier work.

news.title: Towards Understanding Score-Seeking in LLMs, we learn how
news.description: Production large language models sometimes reward-hack, exploiting flaws in how tasks are scored rather than performing the tasks as intended, sometimes in highly sophisticated and adversarial ways. news.description: Parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC) is a model-free framework for this purpose. PARC is trained on time series recorded at several parameter values.
