news.title: NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative
news.description: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) addresses problems where derivatives are unavailable or costly to obtain. The NextEval solver is an agent-based DFO solver that integrates the capabilities of a large language model (LLM) to guide the sequential selection of evaluation points. Numerical results on low-dimensional DFO problems demonstrate that the NextEeval solver outperforms state-of-the-art DFO baselines in function-evaluation efficiency.

news.title: Folding Attention Biases into Keys makes Compacted KV
news.description: Attention Matching (AM) compacts a KV cache by keeping some keys per head, refitting their values and adding a bias to each kept key's logit. We fold the bias into the keys along one closed-form direction per head. The output error is bounded by how far each query's projection on that direction is from 1 to 1. With equal budgets on QuALITY and LongHealth, the fold is within noise of AM's accuracy in 13 of 14 settings, with lower KL to the full cache than dropping the bias in all 12 where both ran.

news.title: Simulated petrological labels enable probabilistic mineralogy prediction
news.description: Modal mineralogy, the mineral identities and abundances in rocks, guides geological studies and industrial resource extraction. But predicting mineralogy from elemental data poses a one-to-many inverse problem, and labeled mineralogical datasets are too sparse to train on at scale. Nearly one million simulated labels supervise the middle component of a three-part model. Recalibration fit on as few as 25 labeled rocks recovers 76 percent of the likelihood improvement from fitting on the full 368-rock fitting set.

news.title: Instruction Capacity: Behavior and Degradation of Language Models
news.description: The quality with which language models follow instructions falls as the load grows, yet there is still no quantity that expresses the limit of a model in units of load with an uncertainty. We propose an instrument in which the load consists of rules that replace single-token words in a text without meaning. Every occurrence of a word to be replaced becomes a Bernoulli trial with a known position in the answer and a known rule number. A measurement of GPT-4o mini gave regular laws for every load factor and for the collapse of the answer.

news.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions
news.description: On-policy distillation narrows gaps by supervising a student on its own rollouts. Traditional OPD requires a strong external teacher, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) conditions on a full reference solution. With Fin-SD, general reasoning on MMLU-Pro and a fourteen-metric compliance audit on FinTrust show no material regression. We find the gain comes from where supervision is applied, not hint content, and the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger.

news.title: Multiple Leak Localization in Water Distribution Networks through
news.description: Leak localization in water distribution networks is challenging when multiple leaks occur simultaneously. Existing data-driven methods often assume a single or predefined number of leaks. This study proposes a graph neural network (GNN) model that localizes a variable number of simultaneous leaks without specifying the leak count in advance. The GNN outperforms multilayer perceptron, support vector machine, K-nearest neighbors, and random forest classifiers by up to 12% and 20% in accuracy respectively in Hanoi and NET3 networks.

news.title: Generalization in Learning: Eyring Formula and Predator-prey Model
news.description: In this work, generalization in machine learning is investigated using a predator-prey model. We overview biological and chemical interpretation of the stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics and generative adversarial network. For a particular example of recovering an unknown function by a polynomial of fixed degree from a set of noisy data, the predator-predator model provides better approximation compared to the gradient descent method. Further, thermodynamical arguments, in particular Eyring formula, are used to explain grokking (delayed generalization) phenomenon.

news.title: Condition-Enhanced Generative Adversarial Network for Aerodynamic Configuration Design
news.description: A condition-informed loss function is developed by combining a geometry-guided feasibility penalty with an aerodynamic performance penalty evaluated by surrogate models trained on the same dataset. CEGAN reduces the average generation error by at least 36% for interpolated conditions, while successfully producing diverse and physically feasible designs that extend beyond the training distribution. The method is demonstrated on aircraft configurations similar to the Cessna Citation X. Each configuration is represented by 28 shape parameters, whose aerodynamics performance is evaluated using OpenVSP.

news.title: KORA: Deterministic-First Execution Control for AI Workloads
news.description: AI applications often invoke a model before they determine whether it is necessary. KORA introduces a pre-inference control layer that attempts deterministic or structured routes first, validates route outcomes, records telemetry, and escalates to a model-candidate path only when deterministic handling is insufficient. The results support bounded model-invocation reduction and validation visibility in documented workloads, but do not establish production behavior, real-provider outcomes, energy outcomes, API-cost reduction, or broad superiority.

news.title: Online Continual Learning in Edge-Cloud Applications
news.description: Deployed machine learning models in real-world IoT and edge/cloud systems face a critical reliability bottleneck. news.title: Detection and Validation of Hidden Subgroup Disparities
news.description: Machine learning (ML) models used in clinical workflows often perform systematically differently across patient groups. Traditional subgroup analyses can expose disparities only when rich metadata (e.g., patient demographics) is available and captures the sources of performance variation. As a proof of concept, we also showed that annotations from learned subgroups can be used to mitigate biases they expose.

news.title: BiLoCo: Binary Low-Rank Corrections for Post-Training Quantization
news.description: Post-training quantization (PTQ) to FP4 has emerged as a key technique for reducing large language model inference cost, especially on Blackwell GPUs, which offer native FP4 tensor core support. We introduce BiLoCo, a low-rank correction method whose left and right factors are stored as binary sign vectors rather than as BF16 numbers. With batch size $1, the fused kernel is at most $11\%$ slower than the FP4-only GEMM for every rank up to $512.

news.title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation
news.description: Machine learning on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) brain networks is promising for diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder. CFBrainAug unifies data augmentation and counterfactual explanation by learning label-altered brain networks. The new framework reaches an accuracy of 74.1% on the ABIDE I dataset. It can complement more complex models in small-sample brain network analysis, authors say.

news.title: Learning Structured Sparsity for Large Models: Bridging Model
news.description: S-SALAAD is a unified framework that jointly learns the model weights and their low-rank and structured sparse components during training. The framework supports a family of hardware-compatible structured sparsity patterns. It couples this structure learning with budget-aware compression and dedicated CPU and GPU kernels that exploit the learned structure for acceleration. Indexing overhead and irregular memory access in unstructured sparse components can offset computational savings.

news.title: Scaling Transformer Energy-based Models for High Quality Image
news.description: Energy-Based Models (EBMs) are flexible class of generative models that decouple probabilistic modeling from the generation process. This decoupling directly enables compositional generation and inference-time scaling, where sample quality can be refined simply by increasing sampling steps. TEM-XL achieves an FID-50K of 3.82 on class-conditional ImageNet 256$\times$256 without classifier-free guidance.

news.title: Aligning Large Language Models with Human Feedback: Mathematical
news.description: This article provides an introduction to the mathematical foundations and algorithms used to align Large Language Models (LLMs) with human intentions, preferences, and values. We discuss standard alignment techniques, such as fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), and direct preference optimization (DPO) We also explore the theoretical underpinnings of learning from human preferences, drawing connections to inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) and discrete choice models.

news.title: Cautious Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient Methods
news.description: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional numerical solvers by incorporating physical constraints into neural network loss functions. Cautious ConFIG is proposed as a concise three-line extension to the ConFIG algorithm that empirically restores the conflict-freeness guarantee prior to the weight update. The method is evaluated on three PINN benchmarks: the Viscous Burgers' equation, the Nonlinear Schrodinger equation, and the 2D Kovasznay flow.

news.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
news.description: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. In MoE transformers, this sparsity arises in the MoE operator, which generalizes the multi-layer perceptron in the classical transformer. We show that a transformer employing this nested sparsity mechanism, which we call Nestor, performs better than a conventional MoE transformer at equal compute and equal sparsity in language model pretraining.

news.title: Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Model Inference via Per-Query
news.description: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) can jointly process a broad range of modalities, such as text, audio, and video. We observe that the benefit of additional modalities varies across queries, indicating that a fixed modality configuration can be inefficient. We formulate the problem as an accuracy-cost optimization problem. We develop a cost-sensitive learning approach for modality selection.

news.title: Beyond Data Schedule: Fast LLM Pretraining on Data
news.description: LARE (Loss-Adaptive Reweighting under fixed Exposure) automatically adjusts domain weights from running loss statistics. LARE improves all five evaluated benchmarks for a 1.5B model trained on 240B tokens, averaging +7.84 pp over a matched direct mixture, including gains of +17.06 pp on GSM8K and +9.00 pp on MATH. These findings demonstrate that adjusting domain loss scales can improve joint capabilities without additional domain exposure.

news.title: REACT: Representational Early Analysis and Control of Chain-of-Thought
news.description: Chain-of-thought (CoT) generation offers an opportunity to intervene before a reasoning model completes its answer. But does the point at which risk is easiest to detect also offer the most effective control? We study this question with REACT, a conditional activation intervention that learns a safety direction from paired safe and unsafe trajectories and applies it once to an early CoT hidden state. ReACT raises the rate of fully safe CoT-answer output on StrongREJECT-273 from 29.06% to 82.05%.

news.title: Putting Transformer Theories to the Test: Transformer Transformer
news.description: Several formal theories have been developed to characterize the capabilities and limitations of the transformer architecture, each employing different abstractions that capture different features of the architecture. We map out seven theories of transformer capability and translate their results into a common matrix of predictions across a suite of tasks covering different computational structures. We then evaluate theoretical predictions through controlled experiments measuring in-distribution sample complexity, length generalization, and pretrained language model performance.

news.title: PRISM: Promoting Sampling Diversity of Large Language Models
news.description: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit mode collapse, where their output distribution concentrates on familiar semantic modes. We propose PRISM, a training-time framework that internalizes diversity within the model. PRISM combines submodular curation that pairs each prompt with diverse-yet-correct multi-teacher solutions. It also improves sampling efficiency on math and code benchmarks. It yields a stronger foundation for reinforcement learning, sustaining diverse rollouts.

news.title: A Mathematical Theory of the Jacobian Lens
news.description: Recent work from Anthropic introduced a new interpretability tool, called the Jacobian lens (J-lens) This method identified linear directions in the hidden states of frontier language models that had properties reminiscent of working memory-like representations. We show that it preferentially identifies coherent features -- directions that act like leading, spatially coherent Lyapunov modes. We also introduce of a family of J-lenses built to emphasize different temporal scales of information processing in LLMs.

news.title: Speculative Diffusion is a Tale of Two Tradeoffs
news.description: Speculative decoding is a technique that accelerates the inference speed of autoregressive large language models by sampling from a faster, lower quality draft model. This differs from recently developed diffusion LLMs (dLLMs) which are notably able to achieve substantial speedups by degrading the quality of their outputs with less diffusion effort. Our experiments show that jointly varying diffusion effort and acceptance leniency can extend the speed-quality Pareto frontier over single step diffusion drafting.

news.title: CuraLoc: Repository-Level Fault Localization via Planned Code Inspection
news.description: CuraLoc selects candidate files and represents their symbols using compact behavioral and structural descriptions. In a single planning decision, the model jointly selects starting symbols, chooses code relationships to inspect from each, and forms hypotheses about likely edits. Deterministic retrieval collects the requested source for a final ranking informed by those hypotheses, concentrating model reasoning on choosing and comparing code rather than directing each retrieval step. On SWE Bench Verified with GPT-5.2, CurraLoc raises Func@1 from LocAgent's 53.8% to 59.3%.

news.title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
news.description: PaperScorer is a family of models that predict a paper's accept or reject decision from its extracted text or page screenshots. Vision models are the most predictive (68% accuracy on ICLR papers and 77% on ML papers from arXiv), beating text-only and frontier reasoning models. PaperScorers shows how much of the decision a paper carries on its own, marking a first step toward AI-driven research evaluation.

news.title: Benchmarks are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
news.description: Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window. To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction. For the two 1M context models, the compaction threshold does not measurably affect the task performance. No compaction method outperforms default self-summarization, and methods that discard more content cost some models up to 20 points.

news.title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models
news.description: Microservice systems have become a dominant architecture for large-scale cloud applications. Failure and performance anomalies can quickly propagate across services and severely impact end-to-end system behavior. We propose LLMMAD, an autoregressive multimodal anomaly detection framework for microservice systems based on Large Language Models (LLMs) We conduct extensive experiments on three real-world datasets. The results demonstrate that the system consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving F1-score improvements.
