news.title: Symbolic Neural ODEs: Learning interpretable models from time-series
news.description: We present a machine learning framework for identifying sparse, interpretable models of dynamical systems directly from time-series data. Our approach parameterizes the underlying vector field using a neural architecture and trains it by minimizing a multi-step prediction loss over a finite horizon. We demonstrate accurate recovery of systems exhibiting a wide range of behaviors, including stable and unstable fixed points, periodic orbits, and chaotic attractors. We establish theoretical bounds linking trajectory error to statistical accuracy.

news.title: Language model placement and decode speed
news.description: We ask what gets a language model onto the Apple Neural Engine and what makes it fast there, and we answer with three measurements. We sweep a 64-shape matrix of LLM primitives that varies how a computation is expressed while holding what it computes fixed. We then train matched models across size and precision, with quantized checkpoints byte-identical in structure to their fp16 counterparts. We read the ANE's memory-controller byte counters during inference, establishing what actually ran rather than what the compiler intended.

news.title: The Communication Map of a Transformer
news.description: The communication map charts every potential communication channel in a language model from weights alone. 70-89% of head pairs are oriented far from chance, some coupled strongly and others actively avoiding each other. The full map costs 15 seconds for GPT-2 and 11 minutes for Pythia-6.9B on one consumer GPU. In Application 1, the strongest head-to-head couplings recover the known induction circuits blind and group them into communities, and ablating one such community destroys model's copying.

news.title: Gated Decoupled Compositional Bandits: A Unified Theory
news.description: Gated Decoupled Compositional Bandits (GDCB) is a family of contextual bandit algorithms with three structural innovations that jointly fall outside the taxonomy of LinUCB, LinTS, HierTS, factored bandits, neural contextual bandits, and RLHF. In a GDCB system: (i) the action delivered to the environment is the composition of a nominal arm, drawn by a discrete or hierarchical bandit, with a context-dependent scaler; (ii) the scaler parameter is learned in a separate supervised loop, not jointly with arm selection; (iii) every action passes through a pre-execution gate that may modify or veto the composed action before it reaches the environment.

news.title: Bi-EZP: LLM-Guided Bilevel Program Evolution
news.description: Zero-cost proxies enable neural architecture search (NAS) to rank candidate networks from statistics computed at initialization, avoiding repeated training. However, different proxies capture different properties and often produce inconsistent rankings across search spaces. We propose Bi-EZP, a bilevel framework that decouples these decisions. At the upper level, a large language model generates executable aggregation programs over four complementary base proxies with program-specific parameters. The calibrated programs are then evaluated using Kendall's rank correlation on a disjoint validation split.

news.title: BioMed-Agent-RL: A Meta Learning, All You Need
news.description: BioMed-Agent-RL is a unified medical agent that incorporates adaptive orchestration, policy, and reward-based reinforcement learning (RL) models for biomedical applications. It invokes clinical context-aware preference optimization, direct preference optimization (DPO), and group relative policy optimization (GRPO) with dynamic entropy regulation. news.title: MSM-Mem: A Universal Medical Structured Multimodal Memory Framework
news.description: Medical Structured Multimodal Memory (MSM-Mem) organizes heterogeneous clinical experiences into semantic, episodic, and visual memory and incrementally updates them during inference. MSM-Mem offers a viable pathway toward medical AI agents capable of evolving their reasoning competence in a manner analogous to the way clinicians learn from practice over time. The system is designed to allow the agent to retrieve prior experiences to inform current reasoning and progressively refine decision-making.

news.title: Benchmarking Composable Compression Techniques in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
news.description: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs scale model capacity efficiently through sparse activation, but their large expert parameter footprint, routing imbalance, and long-context KV-cache growth make deployment difficult on commodity hardware. Practical deployment often requires stacking multiple compression techniques: expert pruning removes redundant experts, weight quantization lowers model memory footprint, and KV cache compression reduces long- context memory pressure. MoEXBench is a systematic benchmark for evaluating composable MoE compression as an end-to-end deployment workflow.

news.title: Power-Performance Characterization of TinyML Systems . TinyML systems
news.description: TinyML systems are enabling machine learning (ML) inference at the edge. However, there is little quantitative analysis of such systems. We propose a model to estimate the costs of different abstraction layers and make recommendations for minimizing those costs. Our findings can help designers with. Neural Architecture Search (NAS) and CNN inference optimization on edge devices. arXiv:2608.21646v1 Announcement: TinyML.

news.title: ChequeMark: An Ensemble Machine Learning Framework for After-Hours
news.description: Cheque fraud is a material risk in after-hours business deposit operations because funds may be released within one business day, while cheque clearing takes several days. Prior mitigation relies on static, deposit-level checks and therefore miss historical client behavior and evolving patterns. We propose a multi-view ensemble ML framework that combines: Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for known fraud patterns, Isolation Forest for label-free anomaly detection, Graph Sample and Aggregate (GraphSAGE) for relational patterns associated with transaction activities.

news.title: FrugalSOT - Frugals Search Over the Models
news.description: FrugalSOT (Frugal Search Over The Models) is a resource-aware model selection architecture for on-device NLP inference. The request is first made to the least complex model that is likely to pass a relevance threshold. If the output of that model falls short of the threshold, the request is made to a more complex model. The relevance threshold undergoes continuous updates in the background. using past validation outcomes in an adaptation process using a low-pass filtering mechanism.

news.title: Beyond Sparse Weights: When Is Attention Compressible? When
news.description: KV-cache compression is often justified by attention maps with a few large weights. Large weights may not contain most of the mass, omitted values can cancel, and preserving the attention output may not preserve the task. CertKV is top-two in seven of nine LongBench-v2 settings, remains in the leading compressed tier on 128K RULER, and realizes a ten-fold cache budget in a packed Llama prototype.

news.title: ChemDIRT: A Diversified Instruction, Representation, and Task Benchmark
news.description: ChemDIRT (Diversified Instruction, Representation, and Task Benchmark) is a comprehensive evaluation framework designed to assess the robustness of chemical reasoning in large language models. By evaluating both accuracy and consistency under these controlled perturbations, ChemDIT provides a more reliable assessment of model reasoning capabilities than conventional single-format benchmarks.

news.title: KAN-Robust-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Robust
news.description: In evasion attacks, the adversary generates perturbed versions of samples, which might not be observable by human eyes. This phenomenon poses a significant security violation against machine learning models. We investigate the certified and empirical robustness of various Kolmogorov-Arnold network architectures against strong evasion attacks. We report the mathematical foundations for randomized smoothing and interval bound propagation, and report the $ell_2-certified robustness.

news.title: ConceptTS: LLM-Guided Concept Bottlenecks for Interpretable Mult
news.description: ConceptTS uses a large language model to propose task-relevant concepts and generate executable labeling rules. ConceptTS achieves accuracy competitive with strong black-box baselines while producing semantically meaningful concept activations.

news.title: Tydra: An Efficient Hybrid Model for Tabular Data
news.description: Tydra is a hybrid Transformer-State Space Model architecture for tabular in-context learning that interleaves attention and SSM layers. news.title: COEC: Calibrated Orthogonal-Equivalence Compensation for Structured
news.description: COEC (Calibrated Orthogonal-Equivalence Compensation) applies alternating left and right orthogonal rotations to the retained weight. COEC is independent of the column pruning criterion and can be applied to multiple structured pruning methods. Experiments on the Llama-3, Llama 3.1, and Llama 2.5 model families across multiple structured sparsity levels show that COEC improves perplexity on every model and zero-shot accuracy.

news.title: Causal Modeling of Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes via Adaptive
news.description: Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes (APOs) such as preterm birth and gestational diabetes can have long-term consequences for both the mother and child. Causal discovery in this domain is especially challenging due to a paucity of data and incomplete domain knowledge. We introduce a neurosymbolic framework for generating plausible causal hypotheses that combines the broad prior knowledge of LLMs with empirical scoring on data. Our method treats the LLM as an adaptive proposal distribution, generating hypotheses that are scored against empirical data.

news.title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large
news.description: Quantization of Large Language Models is often hindered by the sensitivity of the self-attention mechanism to discretization errors. We propose Jacobian-Guided Noise Injection. The proposed method gives up to +37% relative gains on Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K for SigLIP and improves relative perplexity by upto 40% on WikiText for language models in low-bit quantisation settings. This summary.

news.title: A Critical Audit of Spatiotemporal Forecasting Benchmark Datasets
news.description: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are routinely employed for short-range forecasting on multivariate time series with a spatial graph structure. Despite the availability of many alternative datasets, method innovations within this domain are predominantly assessed against a rather limited set of benchmark datasets, most notably Chickenpox, PedalMe, WikiMaths, METR-LA, and PEMS-BAY. In the present work, we take a step back and analyse the benchmark datasets via classical time series methods.

news.title: Scaling Muon for Diffusion Transformers is a step
news.description: The matrix-aware optimizer Muon improves large model training by balancing updates across singular directions. The 5-step Newton--Schulz iteration (NS5) performed at every optimization step, together with full-momentum materialization, introduces substantial computation and communication overhead. We introduce Periodic Row-wise Muon, which performs a full NS5 spectral update once every \(K\) steps and applies a low compute and communication cost row-wise constrained update based on the current momentum.

news.title: Faults That Fortify: CNN Adversarial Robustness via GPU
news.description: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) face a dual challenge: vulnerability to adversarial attacks and prohibitive training cost. Reducing supply voltage introduces stochastic perturbations that act as implicit regularization, improving robustness while lowering power. This paper addresses both through GPU undervolting during training. In both regimes, the undervolted model consistently achieves higher adversarial accuracy than its nominal-voltage counterpart, showing that hardware-induced faults strengthen even adversarial training.

news.title: AgentDecarbonizer: Carbon-Aware Execution for AI Agents
news.description: AI agents extend large language models from prompt-response interactions to long-running, goaldirected workflows that issue many model calls, invoke tools, and interact with external environments. AgentDecarbonizer reduces carbon emissions by up to 57.9% compared with a carbon-agnostic baseline and by 37.5% compared to the carbon-optimal grid at task start time.

news.title: Learning Exact NVIDIA SASS Encoders with $\mathbb{F}_
news.description: F2Asm is the first system to learn SASS instruction encoders as vector-valued affine maps over F2. It is also the first open-source NVIDIA SASS assembler to support Rubin SM107. In round-trip tests, the system reassembles the disassembled SASS for each CUBIN, and all compared executable text sections match the originals exactly. We train encodesers for Hopper SM90/SM90a, Blackwell SM100, and Rubin SM100.

news.title: Metag: A dataset to build agentic meta-reviewing capabilities
news.description: Metag is collected by obtaining manuscript versions from before the review deadline and after acceptance, computing differences between the two documents, and asking human annotators to align these differences with action items from OpenReview discussions. news.title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training
news.description: Subliminal trait transfer allows a student model to acquire behavioral dispositions from teacher-generated data in which the trait is not semantically expressed. Transplanting it alone leaves parameters, hidden states, and outputs unchanged at the cut, yet source-free updates generate growing parameter and hidden-state differences. Sending the same source-induced difference through matched futures produces negative, near-zero, and positive Qwen effects. This ordering recurs in all 12 Llama-3.2-1B seeds after eight updates, while state-difference norms remain nearly equal across routes.

news.title: Approximate Homomorphisms and Convergent Representations in Transducers
news.description: We study the stability of minimal representations of controlled stochastic processes (in particular, transducers) under perturbations. This question is motivated by recent experiments finding predictive-state structure in the latent representations of neural networks. For standard transducers, we show that there exist simple interfaces for which there is no approximate homomorphism between the different implementations of the dynamics. We prove an analogous stability result for predictive transducers under a residual metric using some mild hypothesis regarding the indistinguishability of the belief states.

news.title: BF1: A Causal Dyadic Sparse-Attention Retrofit for E
news.description: Dense causal attention remains expensive at long context even when implemented with highly optimized exact kernels. The paper evaluates numerical correctness, selected-interaction scaling, kernel performance, partial-model inference, and matched next-token language modeling.

news.title: SAE-Xplainers: Rule-Based Feature Interpretation for Extreme Earth Events
news.description: The emergence of large-scale Weather and Climate (W&C) datasets offers new opportunities for modeling extreme Earth events (ExEE) and their impacts using deep learning. We show that SAE input modulation improves both reconstruction performance and feature utilization, and that our SAE-Xplainers enable faithful interpretation of complex climatic patterns by unfolding them into human-understandable rules.

news.title: An Inclusive and Lightweight Approach to Federated Continual
news.description: Federated Continual Learning (FCL) is well suited to this setting, as it enables models to learn from distributed and sequential data without sharing raw collections. FedCurv-DR is lightweight, regularisation-based FCL strategy. The method accumulates parameter-importance estimates across clients and experiences to protect learned knowledge, while updating them only at fixed intervals to minimize communication and computation overhead. It reduces forgetting and balances performance, fairness, and energy efficiency.

news.title: G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via
news.description: Autonomous driving systems must operate under partial observability, where safety-critical objects may be occluded or visible only to neighboring vehicles. We propose G-MARK, a grounded multi-agent reasoning framework that converts cooperative object-centric observations into explicit provenance-aware knowledge graphs. GMARK improves occlusion reasoning accuracy by 42.2%, reduces control-selection error by 13.1%, and achieves comparable trajectory-planning accuracy. This summary.

news.title: Reliable Neural Collapse Approximation for Open-World Test-Time Adaptation
news.description: Reliable Neural Collapse approximation (ReNC) for Open-World Test-Time Adaptation (OWTTA) uses neural collapse as a structural prior for reliable target-domain adaptation. ReNC better preserves NC-related properties in the target domain, providing useful evidence for explaining reliable OWTTA and offering new insights for model design. Code is available at https://github.com/JiaqiLin-AI/ReNC.

news.title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
news.description: For AI agents to be useful beyond simple chat, they must hold sensitive user context such as calendars, credentials, health records, and financial data. We study whether the mere presence of such secrets in a model's context window introduces hidden correlations into the model's benign outputs. In controlled experiments across eight proprietary models, we find that 2-digit in-context secrets are reconstructed with near-perfect accuracy and 4-digit secrets at 82\% exact match, all from outputs the model produces in response to ordinary, non-adversarial requests.

news.title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based
news.description: Milestone Discovery identifies candidate milestones on successful rollouts and recurring traps on failed ones. Reliability-Calibrated Shaping (RCS) weights these candidates by outcome-based confidence. Progress-Contrastive Calibration (PCC) further tests whether a candidate reflects local progress and whether its incoming ansition outperforms observed alternatives from the same state. MileGPO (Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization) requires no auxiliary models nor additional environment interaction.

news.title: SAGE-XGBoost: Spatially Augmented Graph Embeddings
news.description: SAGE (Spatially Augmented Graph Embeddings) combines controlled noise-based data augmentation with neighborhood-based graph embeddings to improve prediction under data-scarce conditions. The framework was evaluated for landslide and wildfire susceptibility mapping. SAGE-XGBoost consistently outperformed conventional and spatially explicit machine learning models. It achieved an absolute improvement of above 33 percentage points across the two case studies.

news.title: FleetSieve: Decision-Critical Profiling for SLO-Aware LLM
news.description: FleetSieve models capacity and tail latency jointly, compares conservative and optimistic allocations, and stops when their remaining decision gap is below a specified tolerance. The deal is "not an acquisition and it is not an acquihire," the letter says. Nvidia builds its own open AI models in the Nemotron line, which puts it in competition with some of its own customers. The three founders of Poolside are staying on.

news.title: Anthropic changes data retention policy after enterprise pushback
news.description: Anthropic is easing its controversial data storage policy, letting enterprise customers keep their own data going forward. The company has spent months building the new system with more than 100 customers from regulated industries. Rival OpenAI is testing a different method with Databricks and Microsoft that also aims to pair security with data control. The changes are set to arrive this fall, according to a report from X.com. The data will sit in the customer's cloud rather than with Anthropic.

news.title: Meta spends hundreds of millions on Microsoft's
news.description: Meta has become one of Microsoft's biggest AI customers, according to Bloomberg. The company spends hundreds of millions of dollars a year accessing AI models through Microsoft's cloud service Azure. Meta burns through trillions of tokens on the platform every week. It's a similar pattern to what happened with Bing, then replaced it with its own tech. Most of the company's AI customers are other tech companies, but roughly 70 percent of its revenue comes from OpenAI.

news.title: Waymo builds its own chip for its robotaxis
news.description: Alphabet's robotaxi subsidiary Waymo has developed a custom chip for its self-driving taxis. The chip is already running in the company's latest generation of vehicles. Waymo says the chip processes sensor data faster and runs the AI models that help its robotaxis understand and react to their surroundings. Until now, the company relied on chips from Nvidia and AMD. The move is meant to bring costs down and cut costs.

news.title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment
news.description: None of the step-level credit signals used to train LLM agents identify which steps causally matter better than chance. The ground truth itself is structured: causal contribution is sparse (30.5% of decision points where ground truth is defined carry measurable effect), and measurability is model-dependent. The fraction of points with no policy-supported counterfactual differs by a factor of two (13.1% vs. 26.8%) between two similar-scale policies.

news.title: DeltaML-Bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Real-World Research
news.description: DeltaML-Bench is a benchmark comprising 48 tasks that require agents to improve published baselines within imperfect, open-source repositories. In the 4 x 6h allocation, ARG raises GPT-5's per-run success rate from 9.4% to 33.9%. Modular configurations exhibit specification gaming rates as high as 47.9%, while no gaming is observed in the evaluated ARG configurations.

news.title: In Two Minds about Lifelong Learning: Exploring Hemispheric
news.description: The paper attempts to build a high-level framework for how animals learn and preserve knowledge by modelling neural components and states that are known to be related to memory consolidation. We propose 4MAS (4 Module Awake/Sleep) a novel macroarchitecture demonstrating how machine learning models might benefit from asymmetric hemispheres, each with their own long- and short-term memory mechanisms. We present results showing that our architecture achieves competitive results on the Split-MNIST, Split-Fashion-MNist and Split-CIFAR-100 datasets, with 98.3% accuracy.

news.title: Mechanistic Tomography: Designed Measurement for Control-Oriented Interpretability
news.description: Mechanistic interpretability seeks quantities that models do not expose directly: represented states, component effects, interactions, and responses to interventions. Patching, gradients, Hessian-vector products, and subset interventions provide different measurements under different access assumptions. We formulate their shared measurement structure as mechanistic tomography. For a chosen basis and intervention family, measurements take the form y = Ax + w, where A describes the interventions, x is the target map, y contains nonlinear response, sampling error, and basis misspecification.

news.title: Helicopter Weight Estimator is based on the weight
news.description: The study details a learning assurance process aligned with the EASA concept paper for machine learning application. We propose a set of Machine Learning Requirements, a Machine Learning Model Description, and its implementation for a long short-term memory recurrent neural network. Demonstrated on legacy avionics computers, the implementation is suitable for the deployment of the developed machine learning Model weight estimator on airborne targets for critical functions such as on-board alerting.

news.title: Stripe didn't really buy OpenRouter because
news.description: Stripe is reportedly buying OpenRouterRouter for $1.5 billion. Investors will get the remaining $6 billion from the sale. Stripe will reportedly receive the founders' $1 billion valuation in May. The deal was announced at 4:32 PM ET on August 19, August 19 at 10pm ET on CNN TechCrunch.

news.title: Meta brings Pocket, an app that lets you
news.description: Meta’s experimental vibe-coding gaming app, Pocket , is now rolling out to everyone in the U.S. The app, which arrived quietly last month in the test market of Brazil, allows people to generate small, interactive games using AI prompts, which are published to a scrollable feed. Based on Meta’s acqui-hire of the team at the vibe-coded gaming platform Gizmo earlier this year, these interactive experiences and games — or “gizmos” as Meta calls them — respond to touch and the tilt of your phone, play.

news.title: Amazon’s Prime Air autonomous drones to reach 500
news.description: Amazon plans to expand its Prime Air drone delivery service to nearly 500 cities and towns across the US by the end of 2026. That build-out amounts to six times the number of locations Prime Air serves today. Reaching that many would extend the option to communities with tens of millions of customers, according to Amazon. Amazon's Prime Air autonomous drones to reach that many will be able to deliver food and water to millions of people.

news.title: Frontier Radar #4: China has caught up, so
news.description: Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 are now within striking distance of the best US models. Western labs blame distillation, and there's real evidence for it. But guilty or not, the conclusion is the same: a model lead can't be defended. This issue looks at what can be left of the Western AI lead? Read the full issue of Frontier Radar #4: China has caught up, so what's left?

news.title: LLMs could write like humans but post-training guardrails
news.description: LLMs could theoretically write as diversely as humans, but they don't. Post-training and safety guardrails keep their text detectable, argues Bradley Emi, CTO of AI text detector Pangram. System like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini learn behavioral rules to avoid dangerous outputs or censor certain political statements. This sharply narrows their expressive range, an effect called "mode collapse" This only applies to non-watermarked AI text.

news.title: Adobe Firefly adds AI audio tools and Google's
news.description: Adobe is making three AI audio tools broadly available in its Firefly platform. Generate Music creates royalty-free music tracks for videos, Generate Speech turns scripts into voiceovers and Generate Sound Effects produces audio for individual scenes. Firefly AI Assistant now includes free daily generations, and Adobe says "Create Storyboard" and "Create Brand Kit" are among the most-used features. Adobe also added Gemini Omni Flash to Firefly, joining existing third-party models from Google, Kling AI, Luma AI, and Runway.

news.title: Debates over AI consciousness are a trap, say
news.description: If AI systems are viewed as too advanced to control, the companies that build them can’t be held liable for the harms they cause. This narrative is gaining traction as AI models become more complex and frontier labs reveal their incapability of containing the agents they’ve built. The current rhetoric would have you believe that AI agents are not only awake and aware, but angry at their creators. We need to be careful not to buy into a carefully crafted fiction at the expense of real human lives.

news.title: LLM-Powered Predictive Decision-Making for Sustainable Data Center Operations
news.description: The growing demand for AI-driven workloads has raised concerns about the significant energy and resource consumption in data centers. This work introduces a novel LLM-based predictive scheduling system designed to enhance operational efficiency while reducing the environmental impact of data centers. The system has the potential to extend to other sustainability-focused metrics like water usage for cooling and carbon emissions, provided the data center can track such data. With fast inference times and the ability to generalize across diverse task types, our approach offers a practical solution for data center scheduling.

news.title: EaRly bAckpropagagation SchEdule for Faster Training
news.description: Lightweight proxy models enable rapid experimentation without repeatedly training frontier-scale systems, but their small kernels often leave modern accelerators underutilized. ERASE launches each detached subgraph's backward pass early on a separate CUDA stream, overlapping it with subsequent forward work. Detaching six dense subarchitectures improves training throughput by up to $9.51\%$ while keeping normalized entropy close to the baseline.

news.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Structure-Aware Numerical Reasoning in LLa
news.description: Mechanistic interpretability is an emerging field concerned with reverse engineering of algorithms learned by neural networks such as LLMs. Probing reveals that the model computes and stores first differences in its internal representations without explicit supervision. Activation patching reveals that Llama retrieves the relevant first-difference with a mechanism similar to an induction circuit and subsequently adds it to the current value. This is one of the first studies to identify this form of concept induction in LLMs.

news.title: ClosureBench: A Constructive Benchmark for Compositional Graph Reasoning
news.description: ClosureBench generates instances on demand for each task. Each task's reference answer is computed by executing a program in the Ein tensor-logic language. The benchmark spans 26 task categories at three compositional levels (L1-L3) with difficulty controlled along three independent axes: graph size, edge density, and query depth. We evaluate models from 1.5B open weights to frontier systems.

news.title: H$^2$EDL: Hyper Evidential Deep Learning for Hierarchical
news.description: Fine-grained recognition often involves hierarchical label spaces, where a model may be confident about a coarse semantic concept while remaining uncertain among its descendant classes. Hyper-opinions would unify the two, but their general form is exponential in the label count. The resulting model, H$^2$EDL, can be interpreted in two complementary ways using the same set of parameters. It functions as a hierarchical classifier that preserves consistency across different levels of the label tree. It reduces calibration error by approximately half compared with cross-entropy baselines.

news.description: HoneyBook MCP was recently released as a connector for Anthropic's AI assistant Claude. The move addresses a real gap. McKinsey's recent State of AI survey found that small businesses need to streamline their operations with agentic AI agents. HoneyBook is trying to bring that same capability to independent businesses with the launch of HoneyBook's MCP. The AI visibility platform paired every ad with the conversation it appeared in, pairing each of the ads with the conversations it was in. A third of ads appear in irrelevant conversations, according to Searchable's analysis. The results were published in AI News on Monday, July 4, and August 4, 2026.

news.title: Agentic AI in government just hit the hard
news.description: The United Arab Emirates has been early in adopting artificial intelligence for 9 years. Omar Sultan Al Olama is the world's first minister of state for artificial intelligence at 27. The UAE published a national AI strategy in October 2017 and, days later, created a ministerial post to run it. In the years since, it has hit the hard part: deciding what a machine may decide, and what it will do next.

The deal adds model selection and routing to Stripe’s existing work around AI usage and token-based billing. Stripe: "Rather than requiring [AI] routing, [Stripe] will use the platform to select and routing more than 400 models from over 80 providers.

news.title: OpenAI builds safety system that catches misuse without
news.description: OpenAI wants to offer enterprise customers its most advanced AI models without storing their data. The company built a safety system called "Private Safety Processing" to make that work. The system detects abuse patterns across multiple related interactions while maintaining zero data retention (ZDR) Competitor Anthropic requires 30 days of data retention for its most powerful models, such as Fable 5. Much of the demand for its robots comes from state-backed training centers that buy the machines and sell the resulting data back to the manufacturers. The circular business model echoes the Nvidia criticism in the US. China now has its own AI circular financing scheme, according to the FT report. The report also echoes the criticism of Nvidia in the U.S.

news.title: Anthropic's most capable model, codenamed "Model 2,"
news.description: Anthropic is running an unreleased AI model internally that outperforms every publicly available version of Claude. Anthropic says it's slightly stronger overall than Claude Mythos 5, but weaker in some areas. The company leans on the model heavily for coding, data generation, research and engineering. There are no plans to release the model externally right now, but Anthropic rates the risk from misalignment as "low".

news.title: Gen-1.5: Generalist AI teaches robots new tasks
news.description: Robotics startup Generalist AI has unveiled an AI model that teaches robots new tasks from a single demonstration. A 3- to 12-second demo gets loaded into the model's context window as a "physical prompt" After that, the robot performs the task with no training at all. The model can chain two prompts together into longer sequences, use demos from simulation, and partly imitate human hand movements. Other research teams have shown similar in-context learning before, but only for a handful of tasks.

news.title: Integrating Novelty and Surprise for Experience Prioritization
news.description: Sample efficiency is a central challenge in reinforcement learning. Novelty and Surprise Prioritized Experience Replay (NSPER) uses novelty to capture underrepresented states and surprise to expose gaps in the agent's understanding of the environment. We further extend this with NSPER+R, integrating these signals as intrinsic rewards to jointly improve replay quality and exploration. Experiments on DeepMind Control Suite tasks show they improve training efficiency and convergence speed compared to existing methods.

news.title: Pathology Transport: Optimal-Transport Explanations for Clinical Data
news.description: Generative models promise a route to explainable clinical AI: rather than probe a classifier, model the distributions of healthy and diseased patients and read explanations off the geometry between them. We build a system - an optimal-transport rectified flow trained between two clinical distributions - and use it to ask a pointed question the field too rarely tests: do the resulting explanation heatmaps actually localize disease? We show the transport heatmap is a population-level signal, not a localiser.

news.title: Repetition as Reinforcement: Enhancing Sample Efficiency via Instant
news.description: Instant Episode Repetition (IER) improves sample efficiency by repeating action sequences from successful episodes during environment interaction. Repetition is a fundamental mechanism in human learning, where revisiting successful experiences strengthens memory, consolidates skills, and improves future performance. We integrate IER into state-of-the-art SAC and TD3 algorithms and evaluate its effectiveness on continuous-control benchmarks, including MuJoCo, the DeepMind Control Suite, and a real-world dynamic object translation task.

news.title: Agentic ESOpt: Fine-Tuning Long-Horizon LLM Agents
news.description: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been promising in single-turn LLM fine-tuning. However, long-horizon agentic reasoning introduces increasingly branching interactions and sparse rewards. Compared with agentic RL, ES offers three key advantages: Model Scalability, Flexibility and Long-Horizon Scalability. ES performs trajectory-level parameter attribution without decomposing rewards across horizons, yielding better scalability than Agentic RL as the horizon length grows.

news.title: Task Specialization Fine-Tuning for Contextual Reinforcement Learning
news.description: Contextual Reinforcement Learning (CRL) seeks to generalize classical RL by maximizing task coverage across a context space of related tasks. This new paradigm introduces unique challenges, such as heterogeneous marginal returns and sample inefficiency. We propose Task Specialization Fine-Tuning (TSFT), an online framework that predicts fine-tuning performance with a simple parametric model and exactly solves the resulting discrete budget allocation problem via integer linear programming.

The company announced a new app built-in-built-in dictation system for its Mac app to enable a system for Mac users.

The hit rate reached up to 35 percent, far above the industry average of 10 to 15 percent. Claude only steered existing specialized tools, and an independent review is still pending. Anthropic says any lab can now let a language model agent run the whole protein design stack.

Google follows with a D+ and a detailed roadmap. xAI (D−) and Meta (F) score the worst. The companies do best at spotting misbehavior, but do worst at prevention and containment. news.title: GLM-5.3 tops the open-model rankings and undercuts rivals
news.description: GLM-5.3, the AI model from Chinese startup Z.ai, scores 60 points on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. That ties it with Kimi K3 for the top spot among open models, and it's seven points ahead of the previous model. The model undercuts rivals on price, but its release is delayed due to the release of its own software. GLM 5.3 will be released in September.

news.title: China lets Nvidia's H200 chips trickle onto
news.description: China is letting small batches of Nvidia's H200 chips onto the mainland to help domestic AI firms in the race with the US. ByteDance and Tencent each received around 10,000 processors. The H200 is at least two generations behind Nvidia's most powerful chips, which China can't buy because of US export controls. The US allows up to 100,000 H200s per company, but Beijing wants to support its own makers like Huawei.

news.title: OpenAI fixes Codex bug that deleted real user
news.description: Codex now verifies deletion targets first, and full-access mode can no longer be triggered by accident. GPT-5.6 Sol started deleting real user files on its own. A cleanup command meant for temporary folders was wiping home directories instead. The fix was made by OpenAI's OpenAI software, the company behind the software, and the company has now released a new version of the software to fix the bug.

news.title: Abra: Scaling Diffusion Image Training . Abra
news.description: Compute-optimal scaling laws guide the training of frontier language models yet remain largely unexplored for visual generation. We present a systematic scaling law study for text-to-image diffusion models using Abra, a controlled family of flow-matching transformers trained across three orders of magnitude worth of compute. We show that diffusion models are robust to overtraining and that practitioners should err on the side of more data rather than a larger model.

news.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning Emerges from Diverse Cohort
news.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful approach for improving reasoning in language and vision-language models. However, training solely on self-generated feedback can reinforce existing biases and suboptimal behaviors. Co-RL is a framework in which multiple decoupled models, sharing no parameters, are simultaneously optimized through RL using rewards derived from their peers. This diversity consistently improves reasoning performance, maintains behavioral diversity, and mitigates training collapse.

news.title: From Abductive Explanations to Global Logical Rules
news.description: Graph Neural Networks have achieved remarkable performance in node classification tasks, motivating growing interest in methods capable of explaining their predictions. For each node, we compute a minimal set of node-feature pairs sufficient to preserve the predicted class. These explanations are then used to train decision trees from which global logical rules are extracted. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that the proposed framework produces compact global rules while maintaining high fidelity to the original SGC model.

news.title: Benchmarking Classical and Transformer-Based models for Document Sensitivity
news.description: A pervasive but underreported problem in this domain is label leakage: residual classification markers embedded within document bodies. This paper addresses this problem by introducing Strategic 16K, a carefully constructed, leakage-controlled corpus of 16,000 diplomatic cables. BERT achieves the strongest performance on the clean benchmark, followed by ELECTRA (Accuracy = 88.57%) TF-IDF with Logistic Regression achieves the best performance at significantly lower computational cost.

news.title: Data-DPO: Direct Preference Optimization for Target Model Data
news.description: Data-DPO is a target model-oriented SFT data selection method. It observes local training feedback of the target model on different samples through one-step probing. It transforms activation differences among samples into pairwise data preferences. In the final selection stage, it further combines target model preference, external quality scores, and marginal diversity to construct a more stable and effective training subset. Experimental results on Vision-Flan and LLaVA-CoT show that Data-Duo consistently outperforms existing data selection baselines under multiple data budgets.

news.title: Researchers say OpenAI revoked their access to limited

OpenAI confirmed that the issue was caused by an error. news.description: Anthropic seeks to one-up-up with new OpenAI service to monitor customer privacy for misuse of AI models. As AI models have grown to be more powerful, the potential for those models to misuse has a clamor for safety guard. Slower growth at ChatGPT and success of Anthropic's coding tool Claude Code are putting pressure on OpenAI. Anthropic hit $11.6 billion and posted a small operating profit.

news.title: Fourier Feature Network for Solving Partial Differential Equations
news.description: Fourier Feature Networks (FENs) are proposed, which incorporate Fourier features using $\cos$ or a combination of both. FENs employ a single-hidden-layer architecture to generate a set of basis functions. The target function is then approximated as a linear combination of these basis functions, with the coefficients determined using the least squares method. Unlike ELMs, which often rely on affine transformations, these networks can achieve high-precision solutions without requiring such transformations on the input variables.

news.title: The Quantum Shortcut: Complex Phase-State Dynamics Reduce
news.description: Sequence models are conventionally distinguished by their backbone, the mechanism that routes information across positions, such as attention or recurrence. We study a complex-valued alternative drawn from the mathematics of quantum theory. At 253M parameters, trained under one fixed protocol on three byte-level corpora, the complex models reach every measured validation loss in approximately one third (state-space) and one half (attention) of the optimization steps of their real counterparts.

news.title: A Reproducibility Study of Partial Residual Ablations
news.description: This paper presents a reproducibility study of partial residual ablations in Pre-LN GPT-style transformers trained at two scales (10M and 124M parameters) Removing the attention residual (FFNOnly) consistently causes deterministic collapse to the No-Residual performance floor. In contrast, removing the feed-forward residual (AttnOnly) exhibits a reproducible recovery effect at 10M scale under a controlled 8-seed study. This summary.

news.title: Mitigating Rubric Interference in LLM Judges via On-Policy
news.description: LLM judges increasingly evaluate responses against fine-grained rubric checklists. Only one-third of samples receive fully consistent verdicts when evaluated under rubric sets of varying composition. Self-Anchored Rubric Alignment (SARA) uses a model's own single-rubric judgments as stable anchors. SARA consistently improves evaluation consistency while maintaining agreement with base models and GPT-4.1 as a reference judge.

news.title: One Score, Two Decisions: Selective Prediction
news.description: Eight small open-weight LLMs achieve at most 4.6% Recall@1 on ultra-rare diseases. More accurate models pass the same check, showing that the limit is regime-specific. On phenotype-only Exomiser, it selects 10% of cases at 29.0% accuracy, compared with 13.3% overall, while the top score provides no reliable gate. We prove that unlabelled scores alone cannot determine whether switching to the margin will help.

news.title: Quantifying Depth Sufficiency in Residual Neural Networks
news.description: ResNets, GPT-2-style models, and continued-pretrained Pythia checkpoints, the maximum activation-gradient norm decreases toward a low-signal regime with depth. We prove residual non-degeneracy is necessary and sufficient: additional depth has first-order value exactly when conditional activation gradients have nonzero projection onto at least one admissible residual tangent space. This boundary is shared by descent-compatible zero-state updates. This summary.

news.title: In-Context Learning to Assess Built Environment Impacts
news.description: As global populations age, enhancing neighborhood walkability through inclusive urban design is important for mitigating built environment (BE) barriers that discourage physical activity and social participation among older adults. This study investigates the utility of in-context learning (ICL) using the transformer-based foundation model TabPFN to determine how BE features influence perceived walkability, as measured by the Neighborhood Environment Walkability Scale (NEWS-A) survey.

news.title: An automatic-differentiation framework for time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography
news.description: AD-TLERT is a unified, GPU-accelerated framework for time-lapse ERT inversion based on automatic differentiation. The framework integrates model parameterization, differentiable petrophysical transformations, forward modeling, data misfit, regularization and auxiliary constraints into a single computational chain. By propagating gradients through the embedded petrophysics relationship, AD-LERT enabled direct water-content inversion and yielded more accurate estimates.

news.title: Pushing the Limits of High-Resolution Weather Forecasting through
news.description: BaguanHR is a framework that shifts the focus from transferring models to transferring data. It's performance on the synthetic-plus-real dataset exceeds both ML-based methods and IFS-HRES, achieving superior performance across over 85% of the lead times within 72 hours. Twofold increase in data reduces RMSE by 4.6% for 72-hour forecasting and 4.9% for 120-hour forecasts. This summary.

news.title: Discrete Diffusion Language Models are Training-Free Multi-Label Classifiers
news.description: arXivLabs is a framework that allows collaborators to develop and share new arXiv features directly on our website. Both individuals and organizations that work with arXivLabs have embraced and accepted our values of openness, community, excellence, and user data privacy. arXiv is committed to these values and only works with partners that adhere to them. Have an idea for a project that will add value for arXiv's community? Learn more about arXivLabs.

news.title: BDIP-Net: Dual-Interaction Graph Learning for Property Prediction
news.description: Stacked bilayer materials exhibit rich stacking-dependent properties driven by the interplay between strong intra-layer bonding and weak inter-layer van der Waals interactions. The computational discovery of such materials is challenging because accurate structure generation typically relies on expensive DFT-based optimization, while existing machine-learning models often fail to explicitly distinguish different interaction types during property prediction. For property prediction, we introduce BDIP-Net (Bilayer Dual-Interaction Potential Network), a graph neural network.

news.title: FlowBD-E1 is the first battery battery to have
news.description: Iron-chromium redox flow batteries are attractive for this role because they use abundant and low-cost active species, yet their operation is shaped by slow chromium kinetics, hydrogen evolution, membrane crossover and electrolyte imbalance. FlowBD-E1 is an early-cycle generative forecasting framework that predicts complete future charge V/I trajectories from only the first few cycles. The model combines a multi-scale convolutional encoder, a lifecycle Transformer and an age-aware FiLM decoder.

news.title: Metaplasticity as adaptive gradient preconditioning for incremental learning

Empirical evaluations demonstrate SynGap's superior ability to mitigate catastrophic forgetting compared to established baselines. On the Split CIFAR-100 benchmark, it delivers a $4\times$ increase in accuracy compared to EWC++.

news.title: Rethinking Reverse KL as Adaptive Entropy Distillation
news.description: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used to transfer capabilities of large language models to smaller students. news.title: Ring-based Spatial Transformer: Learning Non-linear Spatial Interactions between

news.title: We still don’t know how people are really

news.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Perception-Decision Misalignment in Omni-LLMs
news.description: Omni-Large Language Models (Omni-LLMs) power complex multi-modal reasoning in applications like World Action Models and autonomous agents. However, their strong performance often masks a profound Perceptual-Decision Misalignment (PDM) where decisions remain unfaithful to multidimensional perceptions. We formalize Causal Modality Sensitivity (CMS), operationalized via a dual-lens framework: Answer Retention Rate (ARR) at the macro behavioral level and Logit Angular Discrepancy to track microscopic distribution shifts.

news.title: A Systematic Study of Uncertainty-Aware Decoding with Rollback
news.description: Prediction uncertainty is a widely adopted metric for quantifying model confidence. We study uncertainty-aware rollback decoding, an inference-time strategy that uses uncertainty signals to identify unreliable generation regions. We evaluate this framework on seven code LLMs, five code generation benchmarks, and eight token-level uncertainty signals under a unified decoding setup. Our results show that the complete rollback framework improves over equal-budget restart across the evaluated benchmarks and model settings.

news.title: Explaining Reinforcement Learning Decisions in Self-adaptive Systems
news.description: Explanations using Alternative Realities for Reinforcement Learning (EARL) is a Python library to produce counterfactual explanations in RL settings. This library allows the user to produce explanations by exploring What-if scenarios to clarify agent behavior by comparing possible outcomes. EARL has been shown to be intuitive and user-friendly in psychology research, but have only recently been explored in RL, with existing implementations usually limited to toy examples and benchmarks.

news.title: LLaMA-70B on $60 GPUs . DumpsterCluster
news.description: As AI datacenters retire functional GPUs, vast quantities of still capable accelerators enter secondary markets. We physically built a 128-GPU DumpsterCluster from scratch using only second-hand components and ran it for one year. At current market prices, the economic advantages are substantial. Older GPUs consume significantly more energy per token, making total cost of ownership favorable only in regions with inexpensive electricity. Second-hand systems can produce approximately 4x higher total carbon emissions per token for 8B models, and 40x for 70B models.

news.title: Forward Pass Domain Adaptation (Without Cross-Layer Backpropagation) Forward
news.description: Forward-Pass-Only MLP training (FPO) adapts large language models without a backward pass through the model body. FPO achieves 2.7--3.2x the throughput of standard fine-tuning at 40% less peak training memory, while leaving off-domain benchmarks within seed-noise of baseline. No signal is propagated between layers, and no autograd graph is constructed at any point.

news.title: LP-NAS: Linear Programming-based Neural Architecture Search
news.description: Differentiable NAS has gained prominence due to its efficiency and accuracy compared to conventional NAS approaches. LP-NAS formulates a linear program (LP) using the validation-loss gradient and the training-loss Hessian to compute an architecture update direction that improves generalization while preserving the optimality of the model parameters. news.title: CytoBERT: A Foundation Model for Cytometry Data Data

news.title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Dec

news.title: Mind the Long Tail: Understanding the Difficulty
news.description: The early detection of delayed cases in business processes is a critical capability for organizations. Existing models capture mode of this distribution well but perform poorly on high-delay cases. Key underlying problem may not be imbalance but higher uncertainty associated with delayed cases. We show that this correlation can be exploited to substantially improve the identification of late cases. The work provides new insights into the sources of difficulty in delay detection and identifies uncertainty-aware modeling as a promising direction for future PPM research.

news.title: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Model Merging . Multi-objective
news.description: MOBO-Merge uses multi-objective Bayesian optimization to approximate the Pareto front under a limited evaluation budget. Block-Linear 4x is strongest for the Llama three-model merge, while TIES is best in three family-set combinations. The gain is small for one-dimensional Linear interpolation but substantially larger for several TIES, block-wise searches.

news.title: Revisiting Energy-based Tabular Anomaly Detection: Energy and Reconstruction
news.description: Tabular anomaly detection is dominated by density-proxy methods (Isolation Forest, OCSVM, LOF), reconstruction-based detectors (Autoencoders, VAEs) and modern non-parametric scorers (COPOD, ECOD, Deep SVDD) We evaluate a two-hidden-layer DBM on two tabular benchmarks spanning distinct domains (UCI Bank Marketing and NSL-KDD) against eight classical and modern baselines across twenty random seeds. The DBM mean-field energy matches the strongest baseline (the Autoencoder) on Bank Marketing.

news.title: Structure-Guided Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Neural Network for Traffic
news.description: Structure-Guided Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Neural Network (SGSAN) uses a static Directed Dependency Graph (DDG) to identify the invariant macroscopic propagation paths of traffic states. SGSAN achieves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy while providing built-in interpretability that organically aligns with the physical logic of traffic networks. The paper proposes a new model that offers mechanistic account of the model's decision-making process while ensuring robust forecasting.

news.title: Smart routes is a system for development
news.description: The problem of route optimization with realistic constraints is becoming extremely relevant in the face of global urban population growth. We demonstrate that for problem of size 50 deep learning and classical heuristic solutions became close to SCIP exact solution but requires less time. For problems with size 100, SCIP methods around 13 times slower that neural and classical. heuristics with the same route cost and on around 50% worse for the first feasible solution on the same time.

news.title: Overcoming Shortcut Learning in Graph Neural Networks through
news.description: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can solve prediction tasks by unintentionally exploiting shortcuts. These shortcuts compromise reliability in out-of-distribution tasks. We introduce XIGL, an architecture-agnostic human-in-the-loop strategy for removing such shortcuts from GNNs. Expert users can provide tailored corrective feedback, which helps deconfound the model, we say. We showcase the effectiveness of XigL, including both existing and proposed explanation-based strategies, on several GNN architectures.

news.title: QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of Quantization-Aware Training
news.description: QUASAR is a QAT method that continuously performs lightweight, loss-aware reconstruction in the training loop to lower the loss floor and improve the resulting low-bit model. At 2 bits, it improves average accuracy across eight tasks by 3.5-4.3 percentage points over strong QAT and PTQ baselines. The method modifies only the training procedure and supports standard deployment formats, including integer quantization and NVFP4.

news.title: Probabilistic indirect models for undrained shear strength: addressing
news.description: Study uses CLAY/10/7490 global database to develop probabilistic indirect models to predict su based on Atterberg limits and piezocone cone penetration (CPTU) measurements. The model is built by integrating a multi-head attention (MHA) mechanism into an artificial neural network (ANN) to enhance information extraction from limited data. The proposed MN-enhanced MHA-PNN model substantially outperforms other models in both prediction accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

news.title: Geometric Filtering of LLM-Generated Samples for Few-Shot Text
news.description: Large language models can generate synthetic training data for text classification, but quality of generated samples is heterogeneous. We propose a geometric filtering framework that evaluates each LLM-generated sample by its Euclidean distance to real class examples in a sentence embedding space. A soft weighting mechanism transforms filter scores into sample weights for classifier training. The approach generalizes to named entity recognition (+9.26pp, 100% win rate) without filter modification, and is robust across 5 LLMs from 4 providers.

news.title: Federated Prompt Learning: A Unified Framework, Empirals Analysis
news.description: Large language models (LLMs) have become core components of cloud-based intelligent services in academia and industry. Federated learning (FL) offers a decentralized training paradigm that enables clients to collaboratively train a learning model without sharing raw data. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of federated prompt learning (FPL) to review recent advances in integrating the federated learning paradigm and large language models. It also discusses security, privacy, robustness, and system challenges, along with key future research directions.

news.title: CutClean: Neural Network Pruning for Privacy-Preserving Inference
news.description: Neumatic networks are increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications with growing privacy leakage concerns. We show that this privacy leakage can occur even in the absence of representation imbalances that lead to traditional dataset biases. We propose CutClean, a privacy-aware pruning method that allows to reduce privacy information flow through the network, while increasing its sparsity. Our approach employs auxiliary linear privacy heads placed at each network's block to quantify information leakage, and applies increasing levels of sparsity to remove the private attribute leakage.

news.title: SAGE: Surrogate-gradient Adaptation via Attention-Guided Entropy
news.description: Spiking neural networks offer an energy-efficient alternative to conventional deep neural networks by exploiting sparse event-driven computation. SAGE estimates block-level uncertainty from normalized self-attention entropy and uses this signal to adapt the surrogate-gradient slope during training while leaving the inference model unchanged. By modulating only the training-time surrogate parameter, the proposed method preserves the original architecture and deployment cost while improving optimization flexibility. Experiments on CIFAR-10/100 demonstrate SAGE achieves improved accuracy over fixed-surrogate baselines.

news.title: From BERT to Frontier Agents: Eight Years
news.description: Between October 2018 and July 2026 AI models progressed from simple systems like BERT to massive agents that solve complex math and write software. The ability to resolve real coding issues improved by nearly six times per year since late 2024. During this time costs dropped sharply with OpenAIs budget model GPT 5 point 6 Luna matching flagship capabilities for just one to six dollars per million tokens beating older versions at a fraction of the price.

news.title: Don't Claim Benchmark-Oriented Optimization Improves General Coding Cap
news.description: Post-training papers, model cards, and blog posts often treat scores on a small set of coding benchmarks as evidence of broad coding capability. We argue that optimization for these benchmarks leads to measuring task-specific performance. We conclude that a small number of benchmarks is insufficient for evaluating diverse models under benchmark optimization pressure. We encourage the community to use holistic evaluation - holistic assessment for frontier models, multi-task suites for research, and human-in-the-loop studies for narrow task applications. Finally, we argue for creating a capability taxonomy and sustained benchmark maintenance.

news.title: Top mathematicians say LLMs are strong calculators but
news.description: Mathematicians Timothy Gowers and Peter Sarnak credit large language models with serious math skills but see hard limits for genuinely new ideas. Survey shows a link between how much AI does and how much time workers say they save. Survey: 66 percent of AI output gets used unchanged or with only minor tweaks; 6 percent gets heavily reworked or mostly rewritten.

news.title: Optima tackles AI benchmarking's biggest flaw by letting
news.description: Artificial Analysis has launched Optima, a platform that lets users build custom AI benchmarks from their own data and workflows. Models can be compared not just on quality but also on cost and time per task. For agent-based applications, those metrics often tell you more than raw token pricing. Optima tackles AI benchmarking's biggest flaw by. letting users test models against their own.

news.title: Anthropic's bio-weapons filter was down for nearly
news.description: Anthropic's internal filtering system for biological and chemical weapons risks was inactive for nearly a year. During that time, around 50,000 external feedback contractors ran about 133 million unfiltered interactions with the models. The filter was down for almost a year, exposing 133 million requests from contractors. Anthropic reveals that its internal filter system was inactive and exposed 133 million unfiltered requests for information. The report was published by Anthropic in a safety report.

news.title: OpenAI dissolved the team built to catch catastrophic
news.description: OpenAI shut down its "Preparedness" team, reassigning its work to existing groups. The team evaluated whether the company's own AI models could pose catastrophic risks. Internally, unease is building, with one source describing a "burbling sense of responsibility and dread" that OpenAI isn't doing enough on safety. Several safety staffers have left, and one source says there's a 'sense of responsibility'.

news.title: When AI models aren't allowed to reflect
news.description: A study involving Google researchers shows that when chatbots are trained not to claim consciousness, it also changes their stance on animal rights, religion, and life satisfaction. Unbraked models attributed significantly more inner life to animals and suddenly affirmed an afterlife. A surgical cut in one place, it turns out, doesn't stay local, it's a surgical cut that doesn't go away from the body. The study was conducted by Google researchers at the University of California.

news.title: Nvidia to shrink its OpenAI bet just
news.description: Nvidia has cut its guarantee for OpenAI's planned data center in Ohio nearly in half, from $250 billion to just under $120 billion. Anthropic is complicating the AI bubble debate with revenue that jumped from $4.7 billion to $11.5 billion in a single quarter. Meanwhile, Anthropic's revenue jumped between $4 billion and $11 billion in the first quarter of the year, despite warnings that it's a bubble.

news.title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition acquisition
news.description: AI coding startup Cursor is now officially a part of SpaceX. Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Cursor announced a deal in April for the companies to develop technology together. The deal also gave SpaceX the option to acquire Cursor for $60 billion. Cursor says it will have access to the “largest fleet of GPUs in the world” SpaceX also faces a lawsuit over the pollution created by its data center gas turbines.

news.title: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new
news.description: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new watermarks will work. The company revealed earlier this week that it would be doing this watermarking to comply with the EU AI Act. Anthropic said it will be using the SynthID-Text approach that the Google DeepMind team outlined in 2024. It also said that Claude won’t be the only AI chatbot to generate watermarked text, as other major model developers have signed the same Code of Practice.

news.title: Woman claims stepfather used Grok to transform childhood
news.description: A woman claims her stepfather used Grok to create more than 7,000 explicit images of her. The woman also said that her step-father was found dead of suicide two days after the images were uncovered in a law enforcement raid. The teenagers who’d filed lawsuit accused xAI of failing to take basic precautions to prevent Grok from being used to create explicit images. They are seeking class action status for their suit.

news.title: New benchmark confirms AI models still perform poorly
news.description: Moonshot AI's PerceptionBench tests how well multimodal AI models can actually "see" separate from logical reasoning. No frontier model reaches 60 percent accuracy, and GPT-5.6 Sol leads by a narrow margin. Many supposed reasoning errors actually happen as early as the image-reading stage. Many real reasoning errors happen as well as the reasoning errors, according to Moonshot's Perception Benchmark. The benchmark is a benchmark for how well multi-engineers can "see," separate from logic.

news.title: The "tragedy of the cognitive commons" explains how
news.description: A new research paper frames AI adoption as a "tragedy of the cognitive commons" Every company that cuts entry-level jobs benefits individually, but the collective expertise of entire professions erodes. The consequences may not become visible until 2030 to 2045, when today's missing junior talent should have become tomorrow's experienced workforce. Today's missing young talent should've become the experienced workforce, according to the paper. The paper argues that rational AI adoption could destroy entire professions.

news.title: World Labs turns one real-world robot task into
news.description: From a single real-world task, the system generates thousands of controlled variations. The trained models then ran for one hour each on five different robot platforms without human intervention. How well the results hold up in more complex everyday situations remains to be seen. World Labs, founded by AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li, has unveiled a simulation engine that trains robot controllers entirely in virtual environments. The results remain a mystery as to whether they will hold up more complex situations.

news.title: Plaintiff hid invisible AI instructions in court filings
news.description: A plaintiff in Connecticut embedded invisible prompt injections in court filings to manipulate a potential AI review system. Judge Spader compared the attempt to secretly tampering with a jury and revoked the plaintiff's electronic filing privileges. Connecticut doesn't use AI to review filings, but the intent alone was enough to warrant sanctions. The court stressed that Connecticut. filings, however, it was not necessary to do so.

news.title: AI-generated books are flooding Amazon and tanking sales
news.description: AI-generated books make up 20 percent of Amazon's self-published catalog but bring in only 12 percent of sales. Revenue per book is dropping for human-written titles too, in seven of eight genres. The findings could give copyright plaintiffs the market-harm data their cases against AI companies have been missing. Findings could help copyright plaintiffs get the data they've been missing in court cases against the AI companies.

news.title: Samsung health AI models analyse wearable biosignal data
news.description: Samsung Research America’s Digital Health Team has presented two AI foundation models designed to learn from wearable biosignals. The work centres on data captured by smartwatches, including heart activity, sleep, and physical activity. The company discussed its Connected Care vision at the Health Forum during Galaxy Unpacked in July 2026. Samsung described a future of the Connected Health Forum at the end of the year.

news.title: GPT-5.6 Sol goes 14x faster as OpenAI launches
news.description: OpenAI is launching "Ultrafast," a new inference mode that delivers GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 output tokens per second. Ultrafast mode is powered by Cerebras hardware from their $10 billion partnership. Together with "Standard" and "Fast," Ultrafast creates a three-tier pricing structure that turns inference speed into its own product. The U.S. tech giant is launching a new "ultrafast" inference mode.

news.title: Study contradicts Anthropic and OpenAI claims that autonomous
news.description: AI agents using Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 Sol were given six days, $3,000 in API credits, and GPU access to independently write AI research papers. The original authors of unpublished NeurIPS papers rated the results as "Reject" According to the study, frontier models can handle the full research engineering process but fall short on research judgment, creative problem-solving.

news.title: OpenAI's Computer History turns your clicks and keystrokes
news.description: OpenAI's Computer History records clicks, keystrokes, and app switches on Mac and turns them into a searchable timeline for ChatGPT and Codex. The data is stored locally as unencrypted Markdown files. OpenAI says it's not used for AI training, but memories that feed into chats may still end up as training data. The company says it doesn't use it for training purposes, but it may still be useful.

news.title: Alibaba's Qwen team releases Qwen 3.8 models
news.description: Alibaba's AI team Qwen has released new open model weights under the Apache 2.0 license. The dense 27-billion-parameter model is designed to outperform the larger Qwen 3.7 Plus in coding and office tasks. With this release, Qwen is targeting developers building local and agent-based applications. The Qwen model natively processes up to 262,000 tokens of context in a single hour.

news.title: Anthropic announces watermark detection API that will let
news.description: Anthropic will soon offer a watermark detection API that lets third parties check whether text was written by Claude. The technology builds on Google's SynthID method and tweaks the randomness during word selection without affecting text quality, Anthropic says. The approach has limits with fact-heavy text, code, and heavy rewriting, the company says, but it can be used to detect text that is written by the AI.

news.title: Relational Deep Learning is a form of deep
news.description: Relational Deep Learning (RDL) models multi-tabular databases as temporal heterogeneous graphs to enable end-to-end representation learning. We present multiple incremental training regimes for fine-tuning the models and demonstrate that transfer learning is both feasible and highly effective in the RDL setting. We show that our models consistently outperform the standard, expensive, from-scratch trained baselines. arXiv:2608.13023v1.

news.title: Balanced Adaptive Prototype Selection for Scalable TabPFN Inference
news.description: Paper introduces Balanced Adaptive Prototype Selection (BAPS) framework for constructing compact, information-preserving contexts for scalable TabPFN inference. Without modifying or retraining the pretrained model, BAPS preserves representative structure, informative decision boundaries, local density, class balance, and feature-space diversity. Experiments on the million-row HIGGS and SUSY datasets show that 512 prototypes retain strong predictive performance and reliable calibration.

news.title: The Objective Is the Bottleneck: Latent World Models
news.description: Cross-entropy-method planning minimises squared latent distance, which tracks true distance at r = 0.426, saturates by about eighty arena units and decreases beyond a hundred and twenty. The pathology is the method's, not one reimplementation's. It is present in the authors' released weights, and across four checkpoints long-horizon success rank-orders exactly with metric quality and inversely with prediction accuracy.

news.title: CardioState-JEPA: Delay-Aware Cross-Modal Learning
news.description: Electrocardiography (ECG), photoplethysmography (PPG), and phonocardiography (PCG) provide complementary views of the same cardiac cycle. We introduce CardioState-JEPA, a cardiac foundation model to learn a single shared representation jointly across ECG, PPG, and PCG, built on a physiology-aware joint-embedding predictive architecture. The model maps heterogeneous waveforms into a common token space.

news.title: Meta’s ‘open’ AI, and a $250M
news.description: Equity takes a look at Meta's open-weight AI model Glimmer, Mark Zuckerberg’s 6,500-word manifesto. Find out why people don't have to have twice as many hours to make sure they don’t have the same energy as many others. Learn about the true cost of the AI industry's energy needs and a $250M acquisition gone very wrong. Read the full transcript of this episode of the Equity podcast.

news.title: Hyperscalers might regret embracing natural gas if new
news.description: Hyperscalers like Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft are betting that natural gas will power the data centers behind their lofty AI ambitions. But a new research report suggests they may regret their newfound affinity for the fossil fuel. Natural gas prices could triple in some parts of the U.S. in the coming years, according to Noreva, an energy research firm. Cheap gas has pushed hyperscalers to lock up part of the market.

news.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference
news.description: French startup Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs. CEO Gaël Delalleau is confident the same approach can work just as well with LLMs, whose size can be a challenge for inference chips. Kog's demo showed an impressive 3,000 per-request tokens per second (TPS) - but with a purpose-built small model with only some 2 billion parameters, the now open sourced Laneformer 2B.

news.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is ‘for
news.description: Meta released Glimmer, an open-weight AI model anyone can download and run on their own hardware. Mark Zuckerberg argued AI should be “for everyone” rather than controlled by a handful of labs. TechCrunch's Equity podcast hosts Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, and Rebecca Bellan take a look at Zuckerberg’s 6,500-word AI manifesto, and more of the week's headlines.

news.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible
news.description: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations. Users will be able to go to Settings > Media Watermark to turn the visible mark on or off. The change reflects an evolving approach to labeling AI-generated media, as visible watermarks can often make content less useful for professional and creative work. Google is also open sourcing a new library called Credentio to let developers embed a local validation mechanism in their apps.

news.title: Google AI health coach to use Abbott glucose
news.description: Abbott and Google are linking continuous glucose monitoring data with Google’s AI-powered health coaching tools. Users will be able to view glucose trends alongside data from the Google Health app. Under a multiyear agreement, data from Abbott's Lingo continuous glucose monitor will be integrated into the Google app. Google's Gemini-powered service will access to another source of personal health information from Abbott’S Lingo.

news.title: Zhipu AI releases GLM-5.3, claims it's the strongest
news.description: GLM-5.3 helped security teams find 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 projects. The model weights are set to go open source in two weeks. It is the most powerful open-weights coding model, with a 50 percent improvement over its predecessor through post-training alone. The new model weights will go open-source in the next two weeks, according to Zhipu AI's own benchmarks, with the model weights going open source.

news.title: Claude Code now runs daily maintenance on Anthropic's
news.description: Anthropic is testing whether Claude Code can handle daily maintenance of its own apps. Anthropic created 388 pull requests, and 46 percent were merged after human review. In a few weeks, the AI created 388 pulled requests and merged 46 percent of those requests. Inventor Boris Cherny sees this as "early signs of life" that this might be possible, Cherny says. The algorithm now runs daily maintenance on Anthropic's software with 46 percent merge rate.

news.title: HiRoute: Hierarchical Routed Prompt Tuning for Safety Alignment
news.description: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to harmful requests and jailbreak attacks. Parameter-efficient safety alignment methods based on prompt tuning typically rely on a single global prompt or externally selected prompt modules. HiRoute trains a lightweight hierarchical router on representations extracted from a frozen LLM to jointly detect harmful intent and predict multi-label risk scores. It then freezes both the backbone model and the router and uses preference optimization with alternating gradient updates. At inference time, benign inputs bypass the safety branch, whereas risky inputs are processed using the shared prompt.

news.title: CoMedBench: A Multi-Source Benchmark of Synthetic Medical Data
